item.title: Report: Thomas Pieters not on board for LIV Golf 2.0
item.description: Thomas Pieters will not sign up for LIV Golf 2.0 and plans to play on the DP World Tour next year, he confirmed to Flushing It Golf.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Thomas Pieters will not sign up for LIV Golf 2.0 and plans to play on the DP World Tour next year, he confirmed to Flushing It Golf. The 34-year-old Belgian was a member of captain Dustin Johnson's 4 Aces team for the past two seasons in LIV Golf. Pieters is a six-time winner on the DP World Tour, most recently at the Abu Dhabi HSBC Championship in January 2022. He joined LIV Golf in 2023 and reportedly earned more than $25 million in prize money. Pieters competed on the 2016 European Ryder Cup team, posting a 4-1-0 record in a 17-11 loss to the United States at Hazeltine. He joins other notable names who are not returning to LIV Golf as it attempts to restructure without financing from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund. Spanish superstar and three-time LIV Golf individual season champion Jon Rahm tops that list, which also includes Sergio Garcia, Abraham Ancer, David Puig and Adrian Meronk. --Field Level Media

item.title: Amar'e Stoudemire goes from Miami Heat to Miami police officer
item.description: Amar'e Stoudemire has traded in his jersey and shorts for a dress uniform and a badge.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Amar'e Stoudemire has traded in his jersey and shorts for a dress uniform and a badge. Now 43, the former All-NBA player and recent enshrinee to the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame, graduated from the Miami Dade College School of Justice's Basic Law Enforcement Academy on Thursday. He will move into a position as an officer with the county's school police department. On its X account, the college posted photos of the smiling 6-foot-10 Stoudemire with his classmates and teachers. A statement from Miami Dade College explained Stoudemire's motivation. "For Amar'e, this is more than a second career," the school announced in a post on X. "Becoming a police officer was a childhood dream, inspired in part by family members who served in law enforcement. Now, he will begin a new chapter as a police officer with the Miami Dade Schools Police Department, giving back to our community and serving as a positive influence for the next generation." Born in Florida, Stoudemire went straight from high school to the NBA, selected with the ninth overall pick in 2002 by the Phoenix Suns. He was named NBA Rookie of the Year in 2003 and was a six-time All-Star. He played primarily for the Suns and New York Knicks, and briefly, at the end of his career, for the Dallas Mavericks and Heat. In his final NBA season, 2015-16, he appeared in 52 games for Miami. The following season, he played for a pro team in Israel. Stoudemire averaged 18.9 points and 7.8 rebounds over his 846 regular-season games (696 starts). --Field Level Media

item.title: India sets windfall tax on petrol exports at 2.5 rupees per litre
item.description: India has set a windfall tax on petrol exports at 2.5 rupees ($0.0263) per litre, effective October 16, according to a government order issued late on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: India has set a windfall tax on petrol exports at 2.5 rupees ($0.0263) per litre, effective October 16, according to a government order issued late on Thursday. The windfall tax on diesel exports was set at 8.5 rupees per litre, effective October 16, the order said. ($1 = 95.0550 Indian rupees)

item.title: Diesel's surge is starting to push other prices around. Here's how
item.description: The skyrocketing price of diesel is plain for Americans to see anytime they fuel up their cars, SUVs and pickup trucks, though only a fraction of US drivers own a diesel-powered vehicle so they may think they are dodging that massive sticker shock.
item.dc:creator: Dan Burns
item.content:encoded: The skyrocketing price of diesel is plain for Americans to see anytime they fuel up their cars, SUVs and pickup trucks, though only a fraction of US drivers own a diesel-powered vehicle so they may think they are dodging that massive sticker shock. Think again. Wholesale inflation data from the Labor Department on Thursday showed US producer prices climbed far more than expected in September — auguring more stiff inflation at the consumer level in the weeks and months ahead as those costs get passed along. Evidence of the impact of high energy prices, record-high diesel prices in particular, was all over that 34-page readout. Why? Because, as Oxford Economics wrote recently: "Diesel is the workhorse fuel of the economy." Here are some of the ways diesel is driving up producer inflation and how that threatens to drive up a range of consumer costs further soon. GETTING IT TO YOUR DOOR If you own it, eat it or drink it, a truck was involved somewhere along the way in bringing it — either to where you picked it up or to your house. The vast majority of those vehicles in the US goods transportation fleet run on diesel. So when diesel prices more than double as they have over the last year, the cost of moving all that stuff around goes up and soon those shippers begin demanding higher prices for that service. In September, the Producer Price Index's gauge of the cost for truck transportation of freight was up by 19% year over year, the most in just over four years. What's more, those freight transportation costs are responding much faster to the surge in diesel prices than they did to the price surge following the COVID-19 pandemic. That's because the overall economy is in a much better position now than it was then, with the US jobless rate at a still historically low 4.2% supporting robust demand. Also the absolute price of the fuel is more than twice what it was as the pandemic recovery began. FARM TO TABLE Diesel is critical to farming, powering the tractors and harvesting equipment involved in producing food and again in fueling the trucks that take it to grocery stores and restaurants. While end-user consumer food cost increases in both PPI and the Consumer Price Index in September were pretty benign, costs further back in the food supply chain are rising fast. The average of food inputs at stages one and two of what PPI calls "intermediate demand" - which reflect producers' own energy costs and the energy costs embedded in producing key things farmers use like fertilizers and other agricultural chemicals — was up 15.6% from a year earlier in September, again by the most in about four years. Prices for energy-sensitive feed products like corn, hay and hayseeds and oilseeds all shot up by more than 25% year over year. If history is any guide, households should brace for yet higher grocery store prices in the months ahead. "We expect a pickup in food inflation later this year," Oxford's senior US economist Matthew Martin said after the PPI report. ENERGY & CPI The US economy is far less energy-intensive than it was during the oil shocks of the 1970s, but it is still has an impact on prices overall — and more so the longer they stay high. PPI categories like materials for manufacturing — inputs that are themselves absorbing higher diesel costs to produce and deliver — are rising at double-digit annual rates. Producers must take the hit to their margins or pass the costs along. CHRISTMAS IS COMING The diesel surge threatens to make the coming holiday season more expensive — and is already a factor in one of the season's biggest staples: Toys. Prices for toys — exposed to higher shipping costs among other things — rose in September by the most ever month over month.

item.title: Al Pacino recibirá el premio a la trayectoria de la Asociación de Actores
item.description: El célebre actor Al Pacino recibirá el año que viene un premio a su trayectoria por los logros de su vida profesional y su labor humanitaria, anunció este jueves el sindicato de actores SAG-AFTRA.
item.dc:creator: Danielle Broadway
item.content:encoded: El célebre actor Al Pacino recibirá el año que viene un premio a su trayectoria por los logros de su vida profesional y su labor humanitaria, anunció este jueves el sindicato de actores SAG-AFTRA. El actor estadounidense, conocido sobre todo por interpretar a Michael Corleone en la saga de "El padrino", es el sexagésimo segundo galardonado con el Premio SAG-AFTRA a toda una vida de logros. El sindicato le entregará el premio en Los Ángeles, durante la trigésimo tercera edición de los Actor Awards, el 28 de febrero de 2027, en el marco de una ceremonia que transmitirá en directo Netflix. (NFLX.O) El reconocimiento a Pacino llega tras una carrera que abarca más de seis décadas en el cine, la televisión y el teatro. El actor es conocido por numerosos personajes memorables, entre ellos el policía Frank Serpico en "Serpico" (1973), el mafioso de Miami Tony Montana en "Caracortada" (1983) y, más recientemente, el agente de Hollywood Marvin Schwarz en "Érase una vez en Hollywood", la película de Quentin Tarantino de 2019. El premio se entrega anualmente a quien encarne los "mejores ideales de la profesión de actor", según el sindicato. "Me he hecho preguntas y he vagado durante la mayor parte de mi vida, pero siempre me he sentido como en casa con un guión y mis compañeros de reparto", dijo Pacino en un comunicado del sindicato de actores. "El trabajo y los actores con los que he compartido este camino han sido una de las mayores alegrías de mi vida. Es un honor que SAG-AFTRA reconozca esta trayectoria", añadió. Pacino ganó el Óscar al mejor actor por su interpretación del teniente coronel Frank Slade en la película de 1992 "Perfume de mujer", y también ha obtenido múltiples premios Emmy, Tony y Globos de Oro. "Al igual que tantos actores, he pasado mi vida admirando y apreciando esa fuerza de la naturaleza que es Al Pacino. Cuando le ves actuar, estás presenciando a un alumno y a un maestro", añadió el presidente de SAG-AFTRA, Sean Astin, en el comunicado. El actor, de 86 años, nació en Nueva York con el nombre de Alfredo James Pacino. Pasó toda la década de los sesenta luchando por encontrar un trabajo estable antes de que, finalmente, su carrera cinematográfica despegó con "El padrino", de 1972. SAG-AFTRA representa a aproximadamente 160.000 actores, locutores, periodistas de televisión, bailarines, DJ, redactores de noticias, editores de noticias, presentadores de programas, titiriteros, artistas discográficos, cantantes, especialistas, locutores, 'influencers' y otros profesionales del entretenimiento y los medios de comunicación.

item.title: Ｇ７、チョルノービリ原発修復に2.6億ユーロ拠出＝仏財務相
item.description:
[バンコク １５日 ロイター] - 主要７カ国（Ｇ７）はウクライナ北部のチョルノービリ（チェルノブイリ）原子力発電所の修復支援に向け２億６０００万ユーロ（２億９１６７万ドル）の資金を確保した。Ｇ７議長国を務めるフランスのレスキュール財務相が１５日、明らかにした。
レスキュール氏によると、チョルノービリ原発の完全修復には５億ユーロが必要と見積もられており、追加資金の確保に向け１１月９日にパリで支援国会合が開かれる。
Ｇ７はこのほか、ウクライナに対する肥料支援として２５億ドルの拠出も確約した。

レスキュール氏によると、チョルノービリ原発の完全修復には５億ユーロが必要と見積もられており、追加資金の確保に向け１１月９日にパリで支援国会合が開かれる。

French Finance MinisterRoland Lescure said on Thursday in Bangkok that the G7 hadraised €260 million ($291.67 million) for Ukraine to repair itsChernobyl nuclear power plant.    He added that there would be a conference on November 9 inParis to bring together donors and to gather more funds, as thefull recovery of the plant is estimated to cost €500 million($560.90 million).    Lescure said the G7 had also pledged $2.5 billion forfertilisers.

item.title: Indian mutual funds stop bulk subscriptions to gold ETFs ahead of festive season
item.description: Several large Indian mutual funds issued public notices late on Thursday suspending bulk subscriptions to gold exchange-traded funds, just ahead of the festive season when investor demand typically rises.
item.dc:creator: Ira Dugal, Rajendra Jadhav
item.content:encoded: Several large Indian mutual funds issued public notices late on Thursday suspending bulk subscriptions to gold exchange-traded funds, just ahead of the festive season when investor demand typically rises. The notices from the fund houses, including Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund, UTI Mutual Fund and HDFC Mutual Fund, did not cite a reason for the move. There is no restriction on redemptions from these funds. The decision was taken following a nudge from the Securities and Exchange Board of India, according to a mutual fund executive familiar with the discussions. Two bullion industry officials confirmed the halt had followed discussions with the market regulator. The sources declined to be identified as they are not permitted to comment on discussions with the regulator. A spokesperson for SEBI did not respond to a Reuters request for comment outside business hours. The [USN:L1N45X01Q TEXT:"Indian rupee has been under pressure this year"] due to a surge in global oil prices, which have inflated the country's import bill, and heavy selling by foreign investors in Indian equities. Strong demand for gold has further weighed on the currency, prompting the government to raise import duties on gold and silver earlier this year. India, the world's largest consumer of silver and second-largest consumer of gold, relies on imports to meet most of its demand, a dependence that can sometimes widen its trade deficit. Gold imports fell to $1.8 billion in September, from $2.3 billion in August. However, Indians will celebrate Dussehra in October and Diwali in early November, when buying gold is considered auspicious. Inflows into gold and silver ETFs surged during last year's festive season as investors turned to precious metals amid lackluster stock market returns. The move is surprising, as gold and silver imports have fallen sharply over the past two months from a year earlier and have not contributed to the trade deficit, said a dealer at a private bank that supplies bullion to ETFs. "It looks more like a precautionary measure to avoid a surge in imports in October," the dealer said.

item.title: Masiva marcha universitaria contra Milei concluye con incidentes en Argentina
item.description: Una multitudinaria protesta de argentinos contra el ajuste del presidente ultraliberal Javier Milei sobre la educación concluyó el jueves con incidentes con la policía frente al Congreso de la Nación.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Una multitudinaria protesta de argentinos contra el ajuste del presidente ultraliberal Javier Milei sobre la educación concluyó el jueves con incidentes con la policía frente al Congreso de la Nación. Los manifestantes, mayormente estudiantes, docentes y ciudadanos independientes, reclamaban al presidente el cumplimiento de una ley dictada por el Congreso para revertir la reducción del presupuesto universitario, que el Gobierno ha desoído pese a diversos fallos judiciales en su contra. La protesta refleja el profundo malestar de gran parte de la clase media argentina con el ajuste que el mandatario aplicó sobre la economía -en particular sobre sectores sensibles como educación y salud- para reducir la inflación. Ese disgusto se observa en la baja popularidad de Milei que muestra la mayoría de las encuestas de opinión. Autoridades de la Universidad de Buenos Aires (UBA), que cuenta con más de 300.000 estudiantes y varios premios Nobel a lo largo de su historia, estimaron que su personal perdió cerca del 30% de su salario bajo la gestión de la derecha radical. "No normalicemos el incumplimiento de la ley. Las leyes se cumplen. Siempre", publicó en redes sociales la UBA para convocar a la protesta que se desarrollaba frente al Congreso de la Nación. Con inmensas banderas y pancartas a favor de la educación pública, la multitudinaria convocatoria mantuvo paralizado el centro de la ciudad. Pero antes del acto principal hubo enfrentamientos entre la policía y un grupo minoritario situado entre los manifestantes, frente al Congreso, en Buenos Aires, que acabó con heridos y aceleró el fin de la protesta. "Nuestro reclamo es por el financiamiento, por el presupuesto universitario que hace más de 350 días que el Gobierno no cumple. Vamos a seguir luchando por la universidad pública, gratuita y de calidad", dijo a Reuters Juan Sgró, profesor de la Facultad de Artes de la Universidad Nacional de Córdoba. La protesta se replicó en otras importantes ciudades del país como Rosario y Córdoba.

item.title: Martinez apologises for Man United criticism after Carrick talks
item.description: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez apologised on Thursday for criticising the club's hierarchy following their Champions League defeat by Atletico Madrid, after holding talks with manager Michael Carrick and senior officials.
item.dc:creator: Lori Ewing
item.content:encoded: Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez apologised on Thursday for criticising the club's hierarchy following their Champions League defeat by Atletico Madrid, after holding talks with manager Michael Carrick and senior officials. Martinez met with Carrick and club executives after training, two days after saying the club needed greater investment to help the team compete at the highest level following Tuesday's 2-0 loss. "Today I met with the club's leadership and the manager," Martinez said in an Instagram post, in his second statement since the interview. "It was a very positive conversation where we were able to exchange views and speak openly about what happened after Tuesday's game." A club source said that any internal disciplinary action would remain private, adding that it had been Martinez's decision to apologise publicly and that all parties considered the matter closed. Martinez acknowledged that his frustration following the defeat had got the better of him and apologised for choosing the wrong moment to air his feelings. "Everyone knows that I am a passionate person and that I live football with great intensity," he said. "The frustration of the defeat led me to express how I felt at a time and place that perhaps were not the right ones, and for that I want to apologise." The Argentina international had singled out director of football Jason Wilcox in the post-game interview, saying United needed more signings to compete with their rivals and build a squad capable of challenging in Europe. Martinez said his comments had not reflected the unity required at Old Trafford and stressed his belief that everyone at the club was working towards the same goal. "Our club is at its best when we are all united, and I recognise that my words in that moment did not come up with that," he said. "I know that every single person at Manchester United is doing everything possible to achieve our shared ambition, bringing the success that this club and its supporters deserve." Martinez finished his statement by drawing a line under the episode. "With this situation now behind us, we are fully focused on winning together." United are 13th in the Premier League after six games in their worst start in 40 years. They travel to seventh-placed Leeds United on Sunday.

item.title: Judge calls $3,000 hourly rate 'patently unreasonable' as lawyer billing soars
item.description: (Billable Hours is Reuters' weekly report on lawyers and money. Please send tips or suggestions to D.Thomas@thomsonreuters.com)
item.dc:creator: David Thomas, Mike Scarcella
item.content:encoded: (Billable Hours is Reuters' weekly report on lawyers and money. Please send tips or suggestions to D.Thomas@thomsonreuters.com ) A California federal judge approved more than $22.6 million in legal fees this week in a $68 million privacy settlement with Google over its voice-activated assistant, but criticized some of the lawyers' billing rates, including a proposed $3,000 hourly rate that the court called "patently unreasonable." US District Judge Beth Labson Freeman in San Jose refused to accept the $3,000 rate for David Scott of plaintiffs' firm Scott + Scott and reduced it to $1,600 an hour for purposes of calculating the overall class action fee award. "It is not unusual for named partners to charge more than other partners. And the court is cognizant that rates increase year to year. But not to $3,000 an hour," Freeman wrote . Still, the court granted the lawyers' request for 33% of the settlement fund and called the award reasonable and consistent with market rates. Spokespersons for Scott + Scott and the US District Court for the Northern District of California declined to comment. A $3,000 hourly rate may have struck the judge as an overreach in this case, but such figures are no longer a shock among top lawyers at major firms. Reuters has reported [USN:L6N3YQ00F TEXT:"rates as high as $4,000"] for prominent lawyers at Susman Godfrey. [USN:L6N45K07C TEXT:"Gibson, Dunn & Crutcher;"] [USN:L1N3TM04N TEXT:"Milbank"] and Quinn Emanuel are among firms with some partner rates over $3,000. "Lawyers operate in a market, and for better or worse, $3,000 per hour is now very much market rate for top tier partners at large firms," Adam Levitin, a bankruptcy law professor at Georgetown University, said in an email. Levitin and Nancy Rapoport, a fee examiner and law professor at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas, said the courts regularly approve hourly fees in that range for debtors' counsel in bankruptcy matters. Law firm billing rates are typically not public, but lawyers are sometimes required to disclose them in certain cases like bankruptcies and class actions where judges must approve fees. Rapoport said that while hourly rates can attract the most attention, it's the staffing on a case that drives up the costs. "Too many people at a hearing, too many people at a meeting, or the wrong people doing the wrong kind of work. That drives up fees way more than the billable hour," she said. Freeman did not criticize the plaintiffs' lawyers' staffing in the Google privacy case, and said they achieved an "excellent" settlement. Class action plaintiffs' lawyers typically work on contingency and don't receive fees if they lose. Annual billing rate increases are [USN:L1N3UE0PZ TEXT:"key revenue and profit drivers"] for law firms. Hourly rates among large US firms grew by an average of 7% in 2025, according to a report this year by the Thomson Reuters Institute and Georgetown Law's Center on Ethics and the Legal Profession. The Thomson Reuters Institute and Reuters share the same parent company. Scott + Scott said in its July fee request that its rates are partly based on the "prevailing market rates for attorneys and law firms in California that have comparable skill, experience, and qualifications," and defended its rates as reasonable. Scott, managing partner of the 150-lawyer firm, billed about 64 hours as part of the lawsuit, records show, amounting to $194,100 in fees. Another lawyer at the firm, Daryl Scott, billed at $1,960 an hour in the lawsuit, according to billing records the firm submitted as part of its fee request. The settlement resolves claims that Google's Assistant illegally recorded and disseminated private conversations after it was triggered, and used them to send targeted advertising. Google denied wrongdoing, but settled to avoid the risk, cost and uncertainty of litigation, court papers show. A Google spokesperson said the company was pleased to resolve the case. The judge used the hourly rates submitted by the plaintiffs' lawyers as part of her review of the compensation request. She applied a $1,600 rate cap on other plaintiffs' lawyers in the case. Daryl Scott had his hourly rate lowered from $1,960. Geoffrey Horn and Vincent Briganti of Lowey Dannenberg, which also represented the plaintiffs, had initially submitted hourly rates of $1,795. Lowey attorneys declined to comment. ALSO ON BILLABLE HOURS' RADAR THIS WEEK.... --Cornell University hired US law firm King & Spalding to conduct an independent investigation into its policies and procedures following a public outcry over the Ivy League school's handling of an alleged gang rape. But the public may not see the investigation's results, education attorneys told Reuters columnist Sara [USN:L6N45V14Z TEXT:"Randazzo"], because of the risks of exposing the university to more litigation. --2025's white law graduates are securing jobs at a higher rate than their Black, Hispanic and Asian classmates, [USN:L6N46014N TEXT:"according to new figures"] released by the National Association for Law Placement. --Partners are continuing to leave traditional law firms for new startup firms that bill themselves as "AI-native," [USN:L6N46019U TEXT:"including"] the departure of a Goodwin Procter partner to lead a new US law firm associated with Zurich-founded technology company Omnilex AI. Read more: [USN:L6N45R04S TEXT:"Law firms give lawyers time off billing grind to test-drive AI"] [USN:L6N45K07C TEXT:"Thousands of web-tracking lawsuits face extinction under California overhaul"] [USN:L6N45D0X6 TEXT:"Law firms vie for tech talent in AI race"]

item.title: BHP sues union at Spence copper mine over 'illegal' stoppages
item.description: Global miner BHP has sued the workers' union at its Spence copper mine in Chile over two work stoppages it deemed "illegal" because they occurred outside a scheduled negotiating period, a court filing seen by Reuters on Thursday showed.
item.dc:creator: Fabian Cambero, Paolo Laudani
item.content:encoded: Global miner BHP (BHP.AX) has sued the workers' union at its Spence copper mine in Chile over two work stoppages it deemed "illegal" because they occurred outside a scheduled negotiating period, a court filing seen by Reuters on Thursday showed. In the lawsuit, BHP alleged that the mine operations were "significantly" affected due to "two illegal work stoppages" in June and July, and sought compensation of roughly $8.6 million. The union aimed to pressure the mine to pay a special bonus of 5 million pesos ($5,102) per member, which was not included in the existing agreements, the lawsuit shows. The union declined to comment. BHP in a statement confirmed that it had filed the lawsuit. Spence is BHP's second-largest operation in Chile, a country where the firm runs the world's biggest copper mine Escondida. Copper mine unions in Chile, the world's biggest copper producer, often stage strikes to push for better pay and benefits, usually during contract negotiations. ($1 = 979.9300 Chilean pesos)

item.description:
＜ロンドン株式市場＞
続伸して取引を終えた。ヒーリー英財務相が財政規律重視の姿勢を示したことが好感され、ＦＴＳＥ１０...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
欧州市場サマリー（15日） 3:42 配信

＜ロンドン株式市場＞

続伸して取引を終えた。ヒーリー英財務相が財政規律重視の姿勢を示したことが好感され、ＦＴＳＥ１００種は約１カ月半ぶりの高値を付けた。中型株で構成するＦＴＳＥ２５０種指数は０．２６％上昇した。人工知能（ＡＩ）関連株の売り圧力が強まる中、日用品や医薬品株が物色された。

ヒーリー氏は今月発表する予算案は経済の強化を目指すとし、財政規律重視の方針でバーナム首相と一致していると言及した。

製薬大手アストラゼネカは３．２％、ＧＳＫは２．９％それぞれ上昇。日用品のユニリーバは１．８％、ブリティッシュ・アメリカン・タバコは２．５％値上がりした。

ＦＴＳＥ３５０種銀行株指数は０．３０％高。

銅価格の下落を受けて、鉱業株指数は１．３９％安。銅大手アントファガスタは４．１％値下がりした。

製紙・包装大手のモンディは７．９％下落した。

８月の英国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）は前月比０．１％増と、予想に反してプラス成長となった。イングランド銀行（英中央銀行）チーフエコノミストのピル氏は、中銀が今後利上げに踏み切ったとしても、連続利上げの始まりと解釈すべきでないと述べた。ロイター調査によると、市場では１１月会合での利上げ決定を予想している。

ロンドン株式市場：[.LJP]

＜欧州株式市場＞

続伸して取引を終えた。堅調な企業決算が好感された。ヘルスケア株が買われる一方、ハイテク株は売り注文が優勢だった。

スウェーデン通信機器大手エリクソンは６．８％高。直近四半期の業績が市場予想を上回り、買われた。

ＳＴＯＸＸ欧州６００種ヘルスケア株指数は２．３８％上昇。一方、テクノロジー株指数は１．４８％下落。ドイツの半導体製造装置メーカー、アイクストロンは１２．７％安と急落。ドイツの半導体大手インフィニオン・テクノロジーズは５．２％、フランスの半導体材料大手ソイテックは７．７％それぞれ下落。オランダの半導体製造装置メーカーＡＳＭＬホールディングは４．２％下落した。

銅価格の値下がりを受けて、資源株指数は０．８４％下落した。

ＬＳＥＧのデータによると、市場では、欧州中央銀行（ＥＣＢ）が１２月の理事会で利上げを決めるとの観測が強まっている。

欧州株式市場：[.FJ]

＜ユーロ圏債券＞

指標となるドイツ１０年国債の利回りが約５週間ぶりの低水準を付けた。人工知能（ＡＩ）を巡る懸念から株式が売られ、投資家が安全資産の国債に資金を移した。

フランスおよびイタリアの国債と独国債の利回り格差は縮小し、この日の動きが安全資産への逃避だけによるものではないことを示唆した。原油価格の下落も利回り低下圧力となった。

ユーロ圏の指標となる独１０年債利回りは１１ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）低下の３．３５６％。１日の低下幅としては４月以来の大きさとなる見通し。

ここ数カ月、財政の持続可能性に対する投資家の懸念が、特に債務負担の大きい国で国債利回りを押し上げていたが、債券市場の緊張は和らぎ始めている。

仏１０年債利回りは１４ｂｐ低下の４．７３９％。１日の低下幅としては５月以来の大きさとなる見通し。

独仏１０年債利回り格差は４．５ｂｐ縮小の１３７ｂｐ。フランスの財政の先行きへの懸念から、１０月初めには１５８．６７ｂｐと、２０１１年１１月以来の高水準に拡大していた。

イタリア１０年債と独国債の利回り格差は４ｂｐ縮小の１０４ｂｐ。同様に１０月初めには１２９．７４ｂｐと、２０２５年４月以来の高水準に拡大していた。

政策金利見通しに敏感な独２年債利回りは７ｂｐ低下の３．０３５％となった。

item.title: Amazon lanza dos nuevos dispositivos portátiles de escucha y registro información usuarios con IA
item.description: Amazon presentó el jueves dos nuevos dispositivos diseñados para escuchar y registrar la información de los usuarios a lo largo del día con el fin de ofrecerles recordatorios de agenda y otras perspectivas basadas en inteligencia artificial, bajo la marca Bee, que adquirió el año pasado.
item.dc:creator: Greg Bensinger
item.content:encoded: Amazon presentó el jueves dos nuevos dispositivos diseñados para escuchar y registrar la información de los usuarios a lo largo del día con el fin de ofrecerles recordatorios de agenda y otras perspectivas basadas en inteligencia artificial, bajo la marca Bee, que adquirió el año pasado. Frontier es una pulsera y Eclipse es un dispositivo con forma de ladrillo que se asemeja a un cargador magnético portátil. Los usuarios acoplan el Eclipse a sus smartphones. Estos dispositivos recopilan información de calendarios, aplicaciones y otros datos a lo largo del día, según Amazon. La pulsera Frontier cuesta 75 dólares y el Eclipse, 100 dólares, según Amazon (AMZN.O) . "Escuchan todo tu día", afirmó el responsable de dispositivos de Amazon, Panos Panay, en la conferencia TechCrunch Disrupt celebrada en San Francisco. "Te recuerdan las conversaciones que has mantenido, te recuerdan las tareas pendientes que puedas tener y te indican que hay asuntos que te has comprometido a resolver con otras personas". Afirmó que, dado que los dispositivos están siempre escuchando cuando están encendidos, los usuarios no tienen que crear recordatorios por sí mismos y "pueden estar más presentes" a lo largo del día. La empresa señaló que los usuarios controlan la privacidad al decidir cuándo encenderlos y pueden borrar las conversaciones anteriores según lo consideren oportuno. Amazon no almacena el audio. La empresa fue objeto de críticas tras reportes en 2019 que revelaron que miles de personas estaban escuchando las conversaciones que los usuarios mantenían con su servicio de asistente de voz Alexa. Actualmente se enfrenta a una demanda colectiva por esta práctica. Amazon ha negado haber cometido ninguna irregularidad.

item.title: Custom apparel company Custom Ink explores sale, sources say
item.description: Custom Ink is exploring a sale that could value the custom-design apparel and accessories company at close to $1.5 billion, according to people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Abigail Summerville
item.content:encoded: Custom Ink is exploring a sale that could value the custom-design apparel and accessories company at close to $1.5 billion, according to people familiar with the matter. The business, backed by private equity firm Great Hill Partners, is working with investment bank Jefferies on the process, the people said, requesting anonymity to discuss a private matter. Custom Ink, Great Hill and Jefferies declined to comment. The company generates upwards of $100 million of annual earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA), the people said. Schools, teams, businesses and other groups use Custom Ink to design and produce apparel, accessories and other products. Two major players in the adjacent wholesale apparel space merged earlier this year. In June, SanMar Corporation acquired wholesale T-shirt business Bella+Canvas, which [USN:L6N41Y14G TEXT:"was owned"] by the co-founders of popular yoga clothing brand Alo. Those companies sell blank apparel to screen printers and other customers who then decorate and resell the items, whereas Custom Ink works directly with the end customer. Great Hill acquired a significant stake in Custom Ink in 2019 but Custom Ink co-founder Marc Katz remained a major shareholder. Katz, who served as CEO until 2024, and two college friends started the business in 2000 out of a basement in Northern Virginia, where the business is currently headquartered.

item.title: OpenAI y Meta advierten al poder judicial de EEUU sobre el riesgo de fabricación de pruebas falsas
item.description: Expertos en tecnología de OpenAI y Meta Platforms advirtieron el jueves a un comité judicial federal de que los "ultrafalsos" generados por la inteligencia artificial (IA) son cada vez más sofisticados y que resultará cada vez más difícil determinar la autenticidad de las pruebas de audio y video presentadas en los juicios.
item.dc:creator: Nate Raymond
item.content:encoded: Expertos en tecnología de OpenAI y Meta Platforms (META.O) advirtieron el jueves a un comité judicial federal de que los "ultrafalsos" generados por la inteligencia artificial (IA) son cada vez más sofisticados y que resultará cada vez más difícil determinar la autenticidad de las pruebas de audio y video presentadas en los juicios. Los representantes de las empresas y otros compartieron sus opiniones sobre la evolución de esta tecnología durante una reunión celebrada en Boston del Comité Asesor sobre Normas Probatorias de la Conferencia Judicial de Estados Unidos, que lleva tres años debatiendo cómo controlar los riesgos que plantean las pruebas falsificadas generadas por IA en los tribunales. Solo en ese periodo, los rápidos avances en la IA generativa han llegado a un punto en el que los videos falsificados se han vuelto difíciles de detectar tanto para las personas como para el software, señalaron los expertos en la reunión. "Las imágenes generadas por IA no dejan de mejorar, y no creo que en el futuro exista una forma científica de detectarlas", dijo Shira Anderson, asesora de políticas de OpenAI, al comité. El comité lleva desde 2023 debatiendo cómo abordar los problemas de autenticación relacionados con los "ultrafalsos" y garantizar que las pruebas que se sabe que han sido generadas por IA cumplan los mismos estándares de fiabilidad que las pruebas aportadas por un perito humano. El poder judicial ha tratado de adelantarse a pesar de la falta de pruebas de que se trate de un problema generalizado. El Centro Federal del Poder Judicial, el órgano de investigación del poder judicial, señaló en marzo que, de los 931 jueces que respondieron a una encuesta, solo 15 se habían enfrentado a un caso en el que una parte litigante impugnó una prueba por tratarse de un "ultrafalso". "Hay muchos comentarios académicos y de otro tipo que predicen que los tribunales tendrán que lidiar con los ultrafalsos, pero, en realidad, aún no hemos visto muchos casos de este tipo", dijo el juez federal de distrito de Manhattan Jesse Furman, que preside el panel. Sin embargo, expertos del sector, del ámbito académico y del Gobierno advirtieron de que la cuestión dista mucho de ser puramente hipotética. Afirmaron que la capacidad de los tribunales para actuar como filtros frente a las pruebas falsificadas generadas por IA solo va a ser cada vez más complicada. "Los contenidos multimedia generados a partir de modelos de vanguardia, al menos en las últimas generaciones, son indistinguibles para los seres humanos de los contenidos auténticos o generados por IA", dijo Devin Norder, director de gestión de productos de Meta. "Y el costo y el tiempo que lleva crear estos contenidos son realmente insignificantes en este momento". Grandes empresas, entre ellas OpenAI y Meta, han tratado de adoptar herramientas y servicios destinados a verificar la validez del contenido visual, y las nuevas leyes de California y la Unión Europea exigen el uso de "marcas de agua" para detectar los ultrafalsos.

item.title: Trump veta plano do Pentágono de transmitir ao vivo execução militar
item.description: O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, descartou os planos de transmitir ao vivo a execução do ex-major do Exército que matou 13 pessoas em Fort Hood, contrariando o chefe do Pentágono, Pete Hegseth, nesta quinta-feira, depois que a proposta gerou oposição por parte de republicanos, líderes religiosos e da população.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, descartou os planos de transmitir ao vivo a execução do ex-major do Exército que matou 13 pessoas em Fort Hood, contrariando o chefe do Pentágono, Pete Hegseth, nesta quinta-feira, depois que a proposta gerou oposição por parte de republicanos, líderes religiosos e da população. A reviravolta pôs fim ao plano de transmitir a execução por fuzilamento de Nidal Hasan, marcada para 3 de dezembro. O episódio também marcou um raro desentendimento público entre Trump e um de seus aliados mais próximos, embora o Pentágono tenha afirmado que os dois estavam “totalmente alinhados”. Hegseth havia anunciado planos para transmitir ao vivo a execução na base militar de Fort Hood, no Texas, local do ataque perpetrado por Hasan em 2009. Não se tem conhecimento de nenhum outro país que transmita pela TV ou ao vivo execuções judiciais. Trump e seus assessores não estavam cientes do plano de transmissão ao vivo, disse uma autoridade da Casa Branca que falou sob condição de anonimato. “Acho que transmitir a execução para que todos vejam poderia ter sido um forte elemento dissuasivo para o mundo testemunhar como os Estados Unidos lidam com terroristas e escória como Hasan, mas muitas pessoas muito boas e bem-intencionadas preferem não vê-lo morrer, seja por transmissão ao vivo ou por qualquer outro meio visual”, escreveu Trump em uma postagem nas redes sociais. “Ele morrerá, conforme programado, por fuzilamento, mas este evento não será transmitido.” As famílias das vítimas de Hasan poderão assistir à execução pessoalmente, se assim o desejarem, como é praxe nas execuções nos EUA. Alguns colegas republicanos de Trump, incluindo o vice-presidente JD Vance, bem como líderes religiosos, expressaram desde dúvidas até condenação veemente ao plano do Pentágono de transmitir ao vivo. Pesquisas de opinião mostraram que a maioria dos norte-americanos se opôs à transmissão ao vivo. O arcebispo Timothy Broglio, que supervisiona a assistência espiritual dos membros católicos das Forças Armadas dos EUA, também levantou objeções, enquanto o papa Leão condenou a pena de morte em todas as suas formas. Não foi possível entrar em contato imediatamente com um advogado que representa Hasan para comentar o assunto, e não ficou claro se a data da execução marcada para 3 de dezembro seria adiada devido a contestações judiciais. Em um comunicado, o Pentágono informou que Trump conversou com Hegseth sobre a decisão antes de anunciá-la no Truth Social. “O secretário apoia a decisão do presidente, e ambos estão totalmente alinhados”, disse o porta-voz-chefe do Pentágono Sean Parnell. A pena de morte nos EUA já vinha enfrentando um novo escrutínio depois que Christa Pike, condenada por homicídio na década de 1990, sobreviveu a duas injeções letais em uma tentativa fracassada de execução pelo Estado do Tennessee no mês passado, que a deixou gravemente ferida e precisou ser hospitalizada.

item.title: BHP demanda a sindicato de mina chilena Spence por detenciones "ilegales" de producción: documento
item.description: La minera global BHP demandó al sindicato de trabajadores de su mina chilena de cobre Spence por dos paralizaciones "ilegales" de la producción ocurridas entre junio y julio, de acuerdo al documento de la demanda visto el jueves por Reuters, en una medida poco usual en la industria.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La minera global BHP demandó al sindicato de trabajadores de su mina chilena de cobre Spence por dos paralizaciones "ilegales" de la producción ocurridas entre junio y julio, de acuerdo al documento de la demanda visto el jueves por Reuters, en una medida poco usual en la industria. El requerimiento consignado ante un tribunal de la región norteña de Antofagasta detalla que la empresa reclama que el sindicato le pague una indemnización por el equivalente de 8,6 millones de dólares por las protestas no amparadas en el marco legal. "La presente demanda tiene por objeto que el Sindicato repare e indemnice los perjuicios causados a Spence con motivo de dos paralizaciones de funciones ilegales, convocadas y dirigidas por el propio Sindicato los días 30 de junio y 1 de julio (la "Primera Paralización"), y 7 y 8 de julio de 2026 (la "Segunda Paralización"), las cuales afectaron de forma significativa la operación", contempla el documento. Los agremiados exigían un bono extraordinario o compensación que no estaba previsto en el contrato colectivo vigente, según la demanda. Agregó que tampoco estaba en proceso ninguna negociación, que ampara el derecho a huelga u otros mecanismos. El sindicato dijo a Reuters que no tenía ninguna declaración sobre el tema. BHP Spence confirmó a Reuters la demanda y comentó que con ello busca "asegurar la continuidad responsable de nuestras operaciones, por lo que no puede amparar paralizaciones que se desarrollan fuera del marco legal aplicable". En la demanda, la empresa argumentó que la cantidad exigida compensa que debió "activar un plan de contingencia que exigió horas extraordinarias, traslados, alojamiento, entre otros, y sufrió, asimismo, una pérdida de productividad y lucro cesante". Spence, ubicada a 162 kilómetros al noreste de Antofagasta, produjo 254.800 toneladas de cobre en 2025. BHP controla además la gigante Escondida. (1 dólar = 982,5 pesos chilenos)

item.title: OpenAI e Meta alertam Poder Judiciário dos EUA sobre risco de provas “deepfake”
item.description: Especialistas em tecnologia da OpenAI e da Meta alertaram nesta quinta-feira um painel judicial federal dos Estados Unidos de que os “deepfakes” gerados por inteligência artificial estão se tornando tão sofisticados que será cada vez mais difícil determinar a autenticidade das provas de áudio e vídeo apresentadas em julgamentos.
item.dc:creator: Nate Raymond
item.content:encoded: Especialistas em tecnologia da OpenAI e da Meta (META.O) alertaram nesta quinta-feira um painel judicial federal dos Estados Unidos de que os “deepfakes” gerados por inteligência artificial estão se tornando tão sofisticados que será cada vez mais difícil determinar a autenticidade das provas de áudio e vídeo apresentadas em julgamentos. Os representantes das empresas e outros especialistas compartilharam suas opiniões sobre a evolução da tecnologia durante uma reunião em Boston do Comitê Consultivo sobre Regras de Provas da Conferência Judicial dos EUA, que há três anos vem debatendo como controlar os riscos de provas falsificadas geradas por IA nos tribunais. Somente nesse período, os rápidos avanços na IA generativa chegaram a um ponto em que vídeos falsificados se tornaram difíceis de serem identificados tanto por seres humanos quanto por softwares, afirmaram os especialistas na reunião. “As imagens geradas por IA estão ficando cada vez melhores, e não acredito que haja, no futuro, uma maneira científica de detectá-las”, disse Shira Anderson, consultora de políticas da OpenAI, ao comitê. Desde 2023, o painel tem enfrentado dificuldades para lidar com questões de autenticação relacionadas a deepfakes e garantir que as provas reconhecidamente geradas por IA atendam aos mesmos padrões de confiabilidade que as provas apresentadas por uma testemunha especialista humana. O Poder Judiciário dos EUA tem procurado se antecipar à questão, apesar da falta de evidências de que se trate de um problema generalizado. O Centro Federal do Judiciário, órgão de pesquisa do Poder Judiciário, afirmou em março que dos 931 juízes que responderam a uma pesquisa, apenas 15 haviam se deparado com um caso em que uma parte contestou a apresentação de uma prova por se tratar de um deepfake. “Há muitos comentários acadêmicos e de outras fontes prevendo que os tribunais terão de lidar com deepfakes, mas ainda não vimos muitos casos desse tipo”, disse o juiz federal Jesse Furman, de Manhattan, que preside o painel. Especialistas da indústria, da academia e do governo alertaram, no entanto, que a questão está longe de ser puramente hipotética. Eles afirmam que a capacidade dos tribunais de atuarem como guardiões contra provas fabricadas geradas por IA só vai se tornar mais desafiadora. “Mídias geradas a partir de modelos de ponta, pelo menos nas últimas gerações, são indistinguíveis pelos seres humanos das mídias autênticas ou geradas por IA”, disse Devin Norder, diretor de gestão de produtos da meta. “E o custo e o tempo necessários para criar essas mídias são realmente bastante insignificantes neste momento.” Grandes empresas, incluindo OpenAI e Meta, têm buscado adotar ferramentas e serviços destinados a verificar a validade do conteúdo visual, e novas leis na Califórnia e na União Europeia exigem a aplicação de “marcas d’água” com o objetivo de detectar deepfakes. Mas Anderson alertou que, como cada empresa tem seu próprio sistema, não há um meio universal de detectar com confiabilidade todas as marcas d’água ou verificar a autenticidade do conteúdo visual. “Minha impressão é que isso certamente continuará melhorando”, disse ela. “Não acho que algum dia será à prova de falhas.”

item.title: 'Godfather' star Al Pacino to receive life achievement award from actors' guild
item.description: Celebrated actor Al Pacino will receive a lifetime achievement award for his career achievements and humanitarian work next year, the actors' union SAG-AFTRA announced on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Danielle Broadway
item.content:encoded: Celebrated actor Al Pacino will receive a lifetime achievement award for his career achievements and humanitarian work next year, the actors' union SAG-AFTRA announced on Thursday. The American actor, best known for playing Michael Corleone in "The Godfather" films is the 62nd recipient of the SAG-AFTRA Life Achievement Award. The union will present the award to him in Los Angeles at the 33rd Actor Awards on February 28, 2027 as part of a ceremony to be live-streamed on Netflix. (NFLX.O) Pacino's recognition follows a career spanning more than six decades across film, television and stage. He is known for numerous memorable characters, including real-life police officer Frank Serpico in 1973's "Serpico," Miami mobster Tony Montana in 1983's "Scarface" and more recently Hollywood agent Marvin Schwarz in Quentin Tarantino's 2019 film "Once Upon a Time … in Hollywood." The award is presented annually to an actor who embodies the "finest ideals of the acting profession," according to the union. "I wondered and wandered most of my life but have always felt at home with a script and my fellow actors," Pacino said in a statement from the actors' union. "It's the work and the actors along the way that have been among the greatest joys of my life. It's an honor to be recognized by SAG-AFTRA in celebrating the journey," he added. Pacino won the Best Actor Oscar for his performance as Lieutenant Colonel Frank Slade in the 1992 film "Scent of a Woman," and has also won multiple Emmy, Tony and Golden Globe awards. "Like so many actors, I have spent my life in awe and appreciation of the force of nature that is Al Pacino. When you watch him perform, you are witnessing a student and a master," SAG-AFTRA President Sean Astin added in the statement. Pacino also participated in the "America: A Tribute to Heroes" telethon following the September 11, 2001 attacks, and in 2009 received the Arthritis Foundation's Jane Wyman Humanitarian Award for his charitable work. The 86-year-old actor was born Alfredo James Pacino in New York. He struggled throughout the 1960s to find steady work before his eventual film breakthrough in 1972's "The Godfather." SAG-AFTRA represents approximately 160,000 actors, announcers, broadcast journalists, dancers, DJs, news writers, news editors, program hosts, puppeteers, recording artists, singers, stunt performers, voiceover artists, influencers and other entertainment and media professionals.

item.title: Private credit faces deployment squeeze as fundraising hits record
item.description: Private credit direct lenders are raising record sums even as deal activity slows and borrowers return to the banking system's syndicated loan market, increasing pressure to deploy capital into a shrinking pool of attractive opportunities.
item.dc:creator: Patturaja Murugaboopathy
item.content:encoded: Private credit direct lenders are raising record sums even as deal activity slows and borrowers return to the banking system's syndicated loan market, increasing pressure to deploy capital into a shrinking pool of attractive opportunities. Direct-lending funds raised $129.15 billion in the first nine months of 2026, up 35% from a year earlier and the highest nine-month total in Preqin data going back to 2016. Estimated third-quarter lending volume, meanwhile, fell 28% year on year to $49.77 billion, according to PitchBook/LCD. "The fundraising-deployment mismatch increases pressure to put money to work," said Sunaina Sinha Haldea, global head of private capital advisory at Raymond James. She said the mismatch reflected a cyclical shortage of attractively priced deals, compounded by competition from the syndicated market, rather than a structural shortage of borrowers. The divergence is raising questions about how aggressively private-credit managers will compete to deploy capital. Sinha Haldea said plentiful capital and scarce deals could create pressure to concede on spreads, leverage or documentation. Private credit gained market share in recent years as borrowers turned to direct lenders for financing that could often be arranged with greater certainty and flexibility than loans distributed through the syndicated market. That advantage became particularly important when public leveraged-finance markets were volatile. In 2022 and 2023, more loans migrated from the broadly syndicated market into direct lending than moved in the opposite direction, PitchBook/LCD data showed. That balance has shifted this year. Some $16.39 billion of direct-lending loans were refinanced in the broadly syndicated market in the third quarter, compared with just $2.60 billion of syndicated loans moving into direct lending. Tarek Omar, chief investment officer of Royce Stone Capital, said borrowers able to access both markets would naturally gravitate towards cheaper financing once fees and refinancing costs were taken into account. "If the borrowers with more alternatives repay, those with fewer alternatives become a greater share of the loans remaining," Omar said. That does not necessarily mean the borrowers remaining in private credit are weaker credits, since smaller companies may stay with direct lenders because syndicated financing does not suit their funding needs. "The real test of discipline is whether they are willing to leave money undeployed," Sinha Haldea said.

item.title: Williams planeja um ano de comemorações pelo 50º aniversário
item.description: A equipe Williams de Fórmula 1 revelou nesta quinta-feira os planos para uma comemoração durante um ano inteiro de seu meio século no esporte, em 2027.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A equipe Williams de Fórmula 1 revelou nesta quinta-feira os planos para uma comemoração durante um ano inteiro de seu meio século no esporte, em 2027. A Williams, juntamente com a Ferrari e a McLaren, será uma das três únicas equipes a ter completado 50 anos de participação ininterrupta no auge do automobilismo. A equipe conquistou nove campeonatos de construtores e sete títulos de pilotos entre 1980 e 1997. Fundada por Frank Williams e Patrick Head em 1977, a equipe permaneceu sob gestão familiar até 2020, quando foi adquirida pela Dorilton Capital, uma empresa de investimentos privada sediada nos Estados Unidos. Um evento pago chamado “W50 Live”, aberto ao público em Londres de 11 a 28 de fevereiro, apresentará os carros campeões e a história da equipe ao longo de cinco décadas. O carro da Williams para 2027, que normalmente seria o FW49 na sequência e será pilotado pelo espanhol Carlos Sainz e pelo tailandês Alex Albon, receberá o nome de FW50 para comemorar esse marco. Os fãs poderão escolher uma pintura especial para o Grande Prêmio da Inglaterra, corrida em casa da equipe em Silverstone, pista onde a Williams conquistou sua primeira vitória em 1979 com o piloto suíço Clay Regazzoni e também comemorou sua 100ª vitória em 1997 com o canadense Jacques Villeneuve. Entre os produtos especiais estará um conjunto do jogo de tabuleiro Monopoly com o tema W50. (Reportagem de Alan Baldwin)

item.title: Germany warns against bringing Russia back into G20 fold
item.description: At a G20 finance ministers’ meeting in Bangkok, German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil said, “There will be no pretending that Russia is now returning as a normal member of the G20 and simply taking its seat at the table again - not with me, and not with the other Europeans.”
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:

Germany warns against bringing Russia back into G20 fold

At a G20 finance ministers’ meeting in Bangkok, German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil said, “There will be no pretending that Russia is now returning as a normal member of the G20 and simply taking its seat at the table again - not with me, and not with the other Europeans.”

BANGKOK: Germany warned on Thursday (Oct 15) against efforts to bring Russia back on to the international stage, while Britain called for tighter sanctions on Russia n shipping, as questions grow about the strength of US support for Ukraine. Russia n Finance Minister Anton Siluanov attended a meeting of G20 finance ministers and central bankers in Bangkok, just over a month after the US had hosted his first in-person G20 appearance since Russia invaded Ukraine, at a meeting in Asheville, North Carolina. "I do notice attempts, particularly from the United States ... to bring Russia back onto the international stage," German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil told reporters. "There will be no pretending that Russia is now returning as a normal member of the G20 and simply taking its seat at the table again - not with me, and not with the other Europeans."

RIFT OVER RUSSIA SANCTIONS US Treasury Undersecretary Erin Browne said Washington supported Russia's presence, noting that allies had not raised their concerns directly with the US delegation this week. "We think it's really important if you're going to solve a crisis, you need to have open dialogue and open conversation," she told Reuters. "And you can't have ... dialogue, and you can't have resolution to conflict if no one's talking to one another." US President Donald Trump remained committed to bringing about a peaceful end to the war between Russia and Ukraine, she said. British finance minister John Healey called on other nations to tighten sanctions on Russia -linked shipping. "My message to finance ministers here today ... on Ukraine, is to stay the path on tough economic sanctions on Russia , especially a tighter ban on shipping services ... that help ( Russia n President Vladimir) Putin's sanctions-busting shadow fleet to operate," he said. Britain has imposed a series of sanctions on shipping and related services that it believes Russia uses to fund and equip its war on Ukraine.

Related:

Commentary: Trump’s Russian diesel U-turn comes at bad time for Ukraine

Ukraine accuses US of helping Russia as missiles hit Kyiv

NATO general sets out tough military response to any 'foolish' Russian attack

However, a US official said on Wednesday the Trump administration was considering easing sanctions on these vessels, which have transported oil and petroleum products from countries including Russia , Iran and Venezuela. The differences extend beyond sanctions. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said on Thursday that Europe would retain control of Russia n sovereign assets frozen after Moscow's invasion of Ukraine, rejecting any suggestion they could be transferred to a US-supervised vehicle as part of a peace initiative. US President Donald Trump temporarily lifted sanctions on Russia n diesel fuel , a move met with criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, European countries and some of Trump's fellow Republicans in the US Senate. Trump's envoys told Ukrainian officials last week that the diesel deal was part of an effort to draw Russia back to negotiations after the failure of previous efforts to launch sustained talks to end the war. "It is always useful for talks to take place. But I want to be very clear that these talks must not come at Ukraine's expense, or take place over the heads of the Ukrainian people or President Zelenskyy," Klingbeil said.

EU SEEKS TO RAISE FUNDS FOR UKRAINE The EU has pledged €45 billion (US$50 billion) for Ukraine in 2027, but the country's needs will be much higher and the EU is scrambling to organise financial support from countries such as Norway, Switzerland, Canada, Japan and Britain. Klingbeil said he was discussing with international partners how to ensure Ukraine's financing, with commitments from Australia and South Korea made during meetings on Thursday. Healey said Britain would provide £17 million (US$23 million) in funding towards repairs for Ukraine's Chornobyl nuclear power plant, which had been damaged by a Russia n drone strike last year, alongside support from the US and France.

Source: Reuters/fs

item.title: US plan to ease shadow fleet sanctions unlikely to free up many tankers, analysts say
item.description: A potential Trump administration plan to ease sanctions on vessels that have transported sanctioned oil and fuel would likely have limited impact on boosting tanker availability, traders and analysts said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Arathy Somasekhar
item.content:encoded: A potential Trump administration plan to ease sanctions on vessels that have transported sanctioned oil and fuel would likely have limited impact on boosting tanker availability, traders and analysts said on Thursday. Shadow fleet ships still face sanctions from other countries and lack the certification, insurance and maintenance needed to enter mainstream trade. The [USN:L1N46017R TEXT:"discussions"] are the latest in a string of ideas the Trump administration is considering to lower fuel prices and inflation. Tanker rates have [USN:L6N45R160 TEXT:"surged "]in recent weeks because of attacks, higher war-risk insurance costs and complicated operations to move oil out of the Strait of Hormuz that have reduced ship availability. "Kpler expects the measure to have virtually no impact on the current tanker crisis. The proposal assumes that removing sanctions will translate into additional commercially available capacity. In practice, the relationship is far more complicated," analysts at ship-tracking firm Kpler said. Aging vessels, uncertain seaworthiness and unresolved insurance, crewing and management arrangements will limit the ships' commercial appeal, the analysts said. Kpler tracks about 160 supertankers under US sanctions, or about 22% of the commercial fleet. About 46 of them, or 27%, are more than 20 years old. Only about 24 ships could rejoin global trade once age is taken into account and tankers owned by Iran’s National Tanker Company are excluded, Kpler said. "Companies are unlikely to charter tankers that were recently under sanctions as significant risks remain in dealing with vessels. For tankers engaged in Russian trade, EU sanctions still exist while for those engaged in Iranian trade, there is still a lot of liability as the ships were sanctioned for supporting a terrorist organization," said David Tannenbaum, director of sanctions consultancy Blackstone Compliance Services and a former US Treasury sanctions specialist. He added that a lot of ships sanctioned over Venezuela trade were also dealing with Iran, potentially excluding them from easily joining the commercial fleet. The Department of Energy said any move to ease sanctions on the shadow fleet would not help Russia move oil or oil products. "There have been discussions regarding lifting sanctions on dark fleet tankers on an individual basis to allow them to transfer ownership to legitimate operators and move more non-sanctioned oil," said a US official familiar with the discussions, who spoke on condition of anonymity. "This would lower shipping rates and increase flows." However, getting the licenses needed to repossess or sell a shadow fleet tanker typically takes months, if not years, Tannenbaum said. INSURANCE AND MAINTENANCE CHALLENGES Shadow fleet ships also often lack a class certificate, a document from an independent inspection body confirming that a ship and its systems meet technical, safety and environmental standards. Insurers generally require these certificates. Shadow fleet vessels often do not have insurance from credible global organizations, or have insurance from entities set up to cater to the shadow fleet, Tannenbaum said. Insurance tends to be far more expensive for these ships as they are poorly maintained and sail through war-prone regions, traders added. Forward freight agreements — futures contracts that let traders bet on future freight rates — have tumbled on the report that sanctions could be eased on sanctioned ships. Rates to hire an Aframax ship, which can carry up to 750,000 barrels of oil, from US Gulf Coast to Europe fell 30 points, said Scott Shelton, an energy specialist at TP ICAP. The lower freight rates also narrowed the discount of US West Texas Intermediate crude to global benchmark Brent to about $10.42. High shipping costs have hurt US exports, pushing the discount to $14.17 this week, the widest in over five months.

item.title: Leafs D Chris Tanev (upper body) is week-to-week
item.description: Toronto Maple Leafs defenseman Chris Tanev is week-to-week with an upper-body injury, the team announced on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Toronto Maple Leafs defenseman Chris Tanev is week-to-week with an upper-body injury, the team announced on Thursday. He exited in the first period of Saturday's 6-3 win at Colorado, logging just 3:29 of ice time across five shifts after a collision with Avalanche forward Artturi Lehkonen. The Leafs placed Tanev, 36, on injured reserve on Monday, retroactive to Oct. 10, but didn't provide a timeline for his recovery until Thursday. One of the league's most experienced blueliners, Tanev appeared in only 11 games last season due to spine and groin injuries as well as a concussion. Toronto was short-handed before Tanev's injury, in part because general manager John Chayka traded defenseman Emil Andrae to the Columbus Blue Jackets a day before the regular season in a deal that brought star forward Kirill Marchenko to the Maple Leafs. "Tanev's a good player; that's well established, but we have other good players," head coach Jim Hiller said after Thursday's morning skate. "We just have to help them out a little bit." Tanev has recorded 211 points (36 goals, 175 assists), a plus-162 rating and 218 penalty minutes in 884 games with the Vancouver Canucks, Calgary Flames, Dallas Stars and Maple Leafs. --Field Level Media

item.title: フーシ派、サウジの空港など数十カ所に攻撃試みる 戦闘激化＝サウジ連合軍
item.description: [リヤド １５日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[リヤド １５日 ロイター] - イエメンのサウジアラビア主導の有志連合軍は１５日、親イラン武装組織フーシ派とサウジの戦闘が激化する中、フーシ派が今月に入り、サウジの空港、港湾、石油施設数十カ所に対する攻撃を試みたと発表した。

連合軍のトゥルキ・マリキ報道官は記者会見で、フーシ派は今月、サウジの首都リヤドのキング・ハーリド国際空港に対して２０回の攻撃を行い、１７人が死亡、３３３人が負傷したと述べた。同空港はサウジ有数の国際航空ハブで、民間インフラの中で一連の攻撃の標的になっていると連合軍は述べている。

連合軍はまた、イエメン国境に近いサウジ南西部のアブハ空港へのフーシ派の攻撃により、３人が死亡、２８人が負傷したと述べた。

マリキ氏は、フーシ派が弾道ミサイル、ドローン、爆発物を搭載した高速艇など、高度な軍事技術を「地域の勢力」の支援を受けて入手したと指摘。一方、連合軍がイエメンの山岳地帯にある１２７カ所の武器貯蔵施設と発射装置を破壊したことも明らかにした。

その上で、フーシ派に対し、民間人や民間インフラを標的とした作戦を直ちに停止するよう要求。フーシ派は連合軍の声明を注意深く「行間を読んで」理解すべきだと述べた。

連合軍の声明発表後、フーシ派の軍報道官は、サウジの領空と空港は安全ではないと表明し、航空会社への警告を改めて示した。ただし、聖地メッカとメディナ上空の空域は除外するとした。

item.title: Volvo Cars amplía su colaboración con Nvidia en materia de conducción autónoma
item.description: Volvo Cars está ampliando su colaboración con Nvidia para desarrollar una nueva generación de tecnología de asistencia al conductor y conducción autónoma, anunciaron las empresas el jueves, mientras los fabricantes de automóviles compiten por lanzar al mercado funciones de conducción sin manos cada vez más avanzadas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Volvo Cars está ampliando su colaboración con Nvidia para desarrollar una nueva generación de tecnología de asistencia al conductor y conducción autónoma, anunciaron las empresas el jueves, mientras los fabricantes de automóviles compiten por lanzar al mercado funciones de conducción sin manos cada vez más avanzadas. Las empresas indicaron que Volvo (VOLCARb.ST) combinaría sus sistemas de seguridad y su experiencia en ingeniería con las tecnologías de inteligencia artificial y computación de Nvidia (NVDA.O) , entre las que se incluyen el sensor Hyperion, la arquitectura informática y el conjunto de software de conducción autónoma. Alwin Bakkenes, director de ingeniería de software de Volvo Cars, declaró a Reuters que la primera fase se centraría en funciones de conducción supervisada, en las que los conductores seguirían siendo responsables del vehículo. Bakkenes señaló que la ambición de Volvo es introducir gradualmente capacidades más avanzadas, incluida la conducción sin manos en zonas urbanas y autopistas. Esta iniciativa se produce en un momento en que fabricantes de automóviles como Mercedes-Benz, BMW y Ford apuestan por sistemas de conducción automatizada más avanzados, desde la conducción sin manos en autopista hasta la conducción autónoma en condiciones limitadas. Tesla está presionando para que se apruebe de forma más amplia su tecnología de conducción asistida en Europa, incluidas las zonas urbanas, y podría celebrarse una votación a escala de la UE en diciembre. La tecnología debería incorporarse a los vehículos Volvo antes de 2030 y se lanzará simultáneamente en varias regiones, excepto en China, afirmó Bakkenes. Volvo, cuya propiedad mayoritaria pertenece a la empresa china Geely Holding (GEELY.UL), aún no ha elegido un modelo de precios, según Bakkenes, pero las funciones no estarán disponibles únicamente para los modelos de gama alta. Además de Volvo, Nvidia mantiene colaboraciones con una amplia gama de fabricantes de automóviles, entre los que se incluyen Mercedes, Jaguar Land Rover y Hyundai.

item.title: プーチン氏、ウクライナによる製油所攻撃に報復表明＝インタファクス通信
item.description: [モスクワ １５日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[モスクワ １５日 ロイター] - ロシアのプーチン大統領は１５日、ウクライナによるロシア国内の石油精製施設への攻撃に対し報復すると表明した。インタファクス通信が報じた。

プーチン氏は、ウクライナによる攻撃で特に重大な被害は出ていないとしている。

ウクライナはこの日、ロシア国内の製油所を攻撃。これに先立ちウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領は、トランプ米大統領が発表したエネルギー施設への攻撃停止について、ロシアが順守していないとして、ウクライナも応じるのは「終わりだ」と表明していた。

item.title: OpenAI, Meta caution US judiciary about risk of 'deepfake' evidence
item.description: Tech experts at OpenAI and Meta Platforms warned a federal judicial panel on Thursday that AI-generated "deepfakes" are becoming so sophisticated that it will become increasingly challenging to determine the authenticity of audio and video evidence presented at trial.
item.dc:creator: Nate Raymond
item.content:encoded: Tech experts at OpenAI and Meta Platforms (META.O) warned a federal judicial panel on Thursday that AI-generated "deepfakes" are becoming so sophisticated that it will become increasingly challenging to determine the authenticity of audio and video evidence presented at trial. The companies' representatives and other experts shared their views on the evolving technology during a meeting in Boston of the US Judicial Conference's Advisory Committee on Evidence Rules, which for three years has grappled with how to police the risks of fabricated AI-generated evidence in court. In that period alone, rapid advancements in generative AI have reached the point where fabricated videos have become difficult for both humans and software to spot, experts advised at the meeting. "AI images are only getting better, and I do not think that there will be a scientific way going forward to detect them," OpenAI policy counsel Shira Anderson told the committee. The panel has [USN:L1N41K1BT TEXT:"struggled since 2023"] with how to address authentication issues related to deepfakes and ensure that evidence known to be generated by AI meets the same reliability standards as evidence from a human expert witness. The judiciary has sought to get ahead of the issue despite a lack of evidence that it is a widespread problem. The Federal Judiciary Center, the judiciary's research arm, in March said that out of 931 judges who responded to a survey, only 15 had encountered a case in which a litigant challenged the introduction of evidence because it was a deepfake. "There's a lot of academic commentary and other commentary predicting that courts will be dealing with deepfakes, but we haven't actually seen a whole lot of that yet," said US District Judge Jesse Furman of Manhattan, who chairs the panel and on Thursday appointed a subcommittee to further examine the issue. Experts from industry, academia and government warned that the issue is far from purely hypothetical. They said the courts' ability to act as gatekeepers against fabricated AI-generated evidence is only going to become more challenging. "Media generated from frontier models, at least in the last few generations, are indistinguishable by humans from authentic or AI-generated media," said Devin Norder, director of product management at Meta. "And the cost and the time it takes to create this media really are quite trivial at this point." Major companies including OpenAI and Meta have sought to adopt tools and services aimed at verifying the validity of visual content, and new laws in California and the European Union require "watermarking" aimed at detecting deepfakes. But Anderson warned that because each company has its own system, there's no universal means to reliably detect all watermarks or verify the authenticity of visual content. "My guess is that this absolutely will continue to get better," she said. "I do not think it'll ever be bulletproof." Despite those factors, Manhattan US District Judge Valerie Caproni, a member of the committee, expressed caution about the judiciary rushing to craft an AI-specific rule to address the issue, given the lack of data indicating that such a problem was plaguing the courts. She said even if courts began to regularly confront deepfakes, current rules and laws already make it illegal to submit fraudulent evidence and allow judges determine whether evidence was forged. "We've dealt with bad actors presenting fake evidence since Cain and Abel," she said. "That's a longstanding problem." item.title: Congo Ebola outbreak spreads to new province bordering Central African Republic
item.description: The ongoing Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of Congo has spread to a new province bordering Central African Republic, two health officials said on Thursday, posing a fresh challenge for authorities struggling to contain it.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The ongoing Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of Congo has spread to a new province bordering Central African Republic, two health officials said on Thursday, posing a fresh challenge for authorities struggling to contain it. North Ubangi becomes the eighth province to be affected by the outbreak of the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, which was announced in mid-May and has become the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record, with more than 9,000 cases and more than 4,000 deaths confirmed. Two cases have been confirmed in North Ubangi, the officials said. They have not been officially announced by Congolese authorities. Ituri province remains the epicentre of the outbreak though cases have increased recently in North [USN:L6N45H0P8 TEXT:"Kivu"] province. Cases have also been confirmed in South Kivu, Tshopo, Haut-Uele, Bas-Uele and South Ubangi provinces. A health official in North Ubangi told Reuters on Thursday there had been a series of suspect deaths recently in a mining area in Wapinda health zone, close to the border with Bas-Uele, prompting samples to be analysed at a provincial laboratory and in Kinshasa. In addition to spreading within Congo, the outbreak has also resulted in cases in Uganda, which was declared Ebola-free in August, and in Kenya, which announced its [USN:L8N45S0GY TEXT:"first Ebola infection"] earlier this month and announced a second case - a close family member of the first one - on [USN:L6N46011B TEXT:"Wednesday"].

item.title: Carlos Alcaraz accepts wild-card berth in Vienna
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz will compete at the ATP 500 Erste Bank Open in Vienna for the first time since 2021 after accepting a wild card invitation.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Carlos Alcaraz will compete at the ATP 500 Erste Bank Open in Vienna for the first time since 2021 after accepting a wild card invitation. The ATP Tour announced the news on Wednesday. The 23-year-old Alcaraz has had an up-and-down season due to a wrist injury, missing both Wimbledon and the French Open. Still, he has managed three titles, starting with the Australian Open championship, followed by victories in Doha and Tokyo. While Italy's Jannik Sinner is out for the rest of the season due to an injury, a chunk of the Top-10 players are expected in Vienna for the indoor event from Oct. 26-Nov. 1. The field, so far, includes Alexander Zverev of Germany, Russian Daniil Medvedev, Flavio Cobolli of Italy and Australia's Alex de Minaur. In 2021, at age 18, Alcaraz reached the semifinals in Vienna, losing to eventual champion Zverev. Alcaraz is ranked No. 3 in the world and is 33-5 on the season. --Field Level Media

item.title: It’s the economy. But what’s Trump’s answer?
item.description: On two recent reporting trips to Texas, I spoke to supporters of President Donald Trump who said they were frustrated by rising costs but still confident that he can turn the economy around. Yet, less than three weeks before the midterms, Trump is saying little about inflation or how he plans to lower prices. At recent rallies, he has instead attacked political opponents, waxed nostalgic about his first term and taken extended detours into personal grievances.
item.dc:creator: Nandita Bose
item.content:encoded: On two recent reporting trips to Texas, I spoke to supporters of President Donald Trump who said they were frustrated by rising costs but still confident that he can turn the economy around. Yet, less than three weeks before the [TOPIC:"reuters:/world/us/elections/" TEXT:"midterms"], Trump is saying little about inflation or how he plans to lower prices. At recent rallies, he has instead attacked political opponents, waxed nostalgic about his first term and taken extended detours into personal grievances. TRUMP'S ECONOMIC MESSAGE REMAINS A FOOTNOTE Trump has spent more than 16 hours speaking at 13 appearances across 11 states since October 1, by my rough count. But many of the headlines generated by those appearances have had little to do with the cost of living. All 13 appearances aimed to boost Republican turnout ahead of the November 3 midterms. Trump talks about the economy, but rarely for long or in much detail. He touts manufacturing investments, recalls cheaper gas before the Iran war, asserts gas prices were higher under President Joe Biden and promises they will fall once the war ends. In Montana, he dismissed concerns that tariffs fuel inflation, insisting the country has "very little inflation," although the latest government data showed it rising to 3.7% in September from 3.4% in August. He has also pledged $5,000 payouts to all American adults if Republicans win. But the scattered remarks don't add up to a clear affordability message. Democrats have attacked Trump over rising costs, but they, too, have struggled to offer voters a clear economic message. At five recent rallies, Trump repeated a story about spotting gasoline at $1.85 or $1.95 a gallon during a January visit to Iowa. But fuel-price tracker GasBuddy found no regular gasoline that cheap among more than 2,000 stations it monitored that day. The statewide average was $2.57, according to auto association AAA. The anecdote illustrates how Trump's economic message can lean on memories rather than offer new solutions. Even when he addresses the economy, the message often gets lost in his own digressions. In Youngstown, Ohio, Trump went from announcing a submarine-component facility to admiring the jawline of US Senator Jon Husted, an Ohio Republican. In [USN:S0N45A068 TEXT:"Syracuse"], New York, he complained about not receiving the Nobel Peace Prize. In Tennessee, he suggested renaming an ocean after himself. His [USN:L1N45S0W0 TEXT:"Texas rally"] with Senate candidate Ken Paxton made news for protesters, while in [USN:L6N45Z1AD TEXT:"Alaska"], he signed presidential pardons onstage. There are exceptions. At a Baltimore-area shipyard, Trump [USN:L4N45S0Q0 TEXT:"announced"] a $3.7 billion private investment in submarine manufacturing, while a Texas factory visit [USN:L1N45M0V2 TEXT:"highlighted"] jobs and tariffs. Both generated economic coverage. But unlike his sprawling rallies, those visits were built around specific announcements. The political backdrop is getting tougher for Republicans – recent [USN:L4N45T027 TEXT:"polling"] has added to concerns about their ability to hold on to Congress. With Republicans increasingly relying on Trump to rally their voters, his appearances have taken on greater importance. But they also mean the president, rather than the candidates themselves, often determines what gets talked about in the final weeks of the campaign. He repeatedly tells supporters to pretend he is on the ballot, hoping to mobilize voters who might otherwise skip the midterms. In close races, that could matter. But firing up the base is only part of the task. Republicans also need to attract voters unhappy with the economy who aren't committed to either party. They may never attend a Trump rally, but they'll see the headlines. TOP US POLITICS HEADLINES Special Report: In Trump’s pardons for public officials, Republicans win most of the mercy [USN:L6N45Y0SX TEXT:"Musk has spent $276 million on midterms to help Republicans retain control of Congress"] [USN:L6N45T19V TEXT:"The midterm strategy driving Democrats deep into Trump country"] [USN:L1N45V0SB TEXT:"Ohio's working-class voters rethink support for Trump and the Republican Party"] [USN:L4N45Y17K TEXT:"Inside the booming market for US midterm election bets"] [USN:L4N45K1IR TEXT:"Democratic midterm wins could bring scrutiny for Wall Street, crypto firms"] [USN:L1N4610D7 TEXT:"Just over half of candidates in key US Senate races say they will accept results, others hedge"] POLL OF THE WEEK THE VIEW FROM ROME Trump's effort to lower energy prices ahead of the midterms is creating friction with a close European ally. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni called a US-Russia diesel deal [USN:S8N43U03J TEXT:"a "very risky choice""] on Wednesday, warning it could undermine efforts to pressure Moscow into ending its war in Ukraine. Trump has [USN:S0N435010 TEXT:"defended"] the arrangement, saying it would lower energy costs, but European leaders worry it could provide Russia with revenue while weakening sanctions.
