item.title: 英ＧＤＰ、8月は前月比0.1％増 ＡＩブームが押し上げ
item.description:
Andy Bruce
[マンチェスター（英国）１５日 ロイター] - 英国立統計局（ＯＮＳ）が１５日発表した８月の国...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
英ＧＤＰ、8月は前月比0.1％増　ＡＩブームが押し上げ 10/15 16:35 配信

ロンドンのカナリーワーフで2025年9月撮影。 REUTERS/Toby Melville

Andy Bruce

[マンチェスター（英国）１５日 ロイター] - 英国立統計局（ＯＮＳ）が１５日発表した８月の国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）は前月比０．１％増と、予想に反してプラス成長となった。コンピュータープログラミング部門が一段と伸び、人工知能（ＡＩ）が成長を押し上げていることを示す形となった。

ロイターがまとめたエコノミスト予想は０．１％減だった。

前年同月比の成長率は２．１％に加速し、新型コロナウイルス禍から経済が回復していた２０２２年１０月以来の高水準となった。この時期を除けば、１９年１２月以来の高い伸びだった。

＜英経済、幅広い分野で力強さ＞

ＯＮＳは英経済の大部分を占めるサービス業で、過去１年間に幅広い分野が成長したと指摘した。

ＲＳＭ ＵＫのチーフエコノミストのトーマス・ピュー氏は「第４・四半期に経済活動が停滞したとしても、今年の経済を底堅いと表現するのはやめて、十分に評価できる成長を遂げたと語るべきだろう」と述べた。

第３・四半期の成長率はイングランド銀行（英中央銀行）の予測である０．４％を上回る見通しとなっており、今回の統計は１１月の会合で利上げについて検討する当局者の判断にも影響する可能性がある。

ピュー氏は、現在の金利水準が経済活動を抑える効果は、英中銀が想定していたほど強くないことが示唆されたと語った。

ヒーリー財務相は今回の統計について声明で「中東や欧州での紛争が世界中の人々に打撃を与えているが、きょうの統計はこうした世界的な衝撃に対する英国の底堅さを改めて示している」と述べた。

＜製造業がけん引、プログラミングも急伸＞

８月単月では製造業が成長をけん引した。製造業の生産は小幅減少の予想に反し、前月比１．２％の大幅増となった。

サービス業は横ばいだったが、０．１％減との予想を上回った。コンピュータープログラミングが再び目立った伸びを示し、１．１％増加した。年初からの増加率は１３％に達した。６─８月の成長への寄与も最大だった。建設業の生産は小幅に減少した。

ＰｗＣのシニアエコノミスト、ジェイク・フィニー氏は、今年の英経済が予想外に力強く成長している重要な要因として、企業の設備投資、特に情報技術関連のハードウエアへの投資を挙げた。「英国は投資の規模でも、投資が成長を押し上げる効果でも、依然として米国に後れを取っている。ただ前進しており、欧州の多くの国に引き続き先行している」と述べた。

ベレンバーグのシニアエコノミスト、アンドリュー・ウィシャート氏は「部門別の内訳を見ると、景気の上向きの大部分はＡＩによるものとみられる」と述べ、インフレが加速しているにもかかわらず、個人消費も予想を上回ったした。

ロイター 関連ニュース 焦点：債務膨張の先進国に金融危機の芽、最も懸念される米・伊・英 アングル：英新財務相、実務手腕に一定評価も支出拡大・増税不安消えず アングル：英国経済、ＥＵ離脱から10年の軌跡 アングル：ブレグジット10年、英ＥＵの溝なお深く　極右台頭も重し 焦点：ＥＵ離脱から10年、苦闘続く英輸出企業　非離脱シナリオより低成長の予測 最終更新: 10/15(木) 18:03 ロイター

item.title: アジア株式市場サマリー：引け（15日）
item.description: 中国市場は下落し１４カ月ぶりの安値で引けた。予想を上回る米インフレ指標を受けて追加利上げ観測が強まり、ハイテク株を中心に...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
アジア株式市場サマリー：引け（15日） 10/15 16:33 配信

中国市場は下落し１４カ月ぶりの安値で引けた。予想を上回る米インフレ指標を受けて追加利上げ観測が強まり、ハイテク株を中心に世界的に株安が広がった流れを引き継いだ。

上海総合指数とＣＳＩ３００指数はともに１．６％下落。いずれも２０２５年８月以来の安値で引けた。

上海証券取引所の新興ハイテク企業向け市場「科創板」５０指数は１．５％安、深セン証券取引所の新興企業向け市場「創業板（チャイネクスト）」総合指数は２．９％下落した。

ＵＢＳ証券の中国株ストラテジスト、レイ・モン氏は「最近の調整は、過熱していたハイテク株の持ち高解消が集中的に進んだことが主因とみられる。投資信託も、元本回復時の解約に関連した圧力に直面している」と指摘。「地政学リスク、米国債利回り、原油価格のボラティリティーがインフレ期待に影響を及ぼし、ドルの流動性が引き締まった結果、市場のリスク選好を圧迫している」と指摘した。

前日の米国市場では、消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）が予想を上回る伸びとなり、米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）が利上げに動く可能性があるとの観測が一時再燃したことで、ドルが上昇する一方、米株は下落した。

投資家の関心は１９日に発表される中国の第３・四半期国内総生産（ＧＤＰ）統計に向かっている。貿易から融資まで一連の指標が好調だった中、景気回復の勢いを見極める材料となる。

国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）は１５日、アジアの経済成長が２０２７年に減速するとの見通しを示した。イラン戦争に伴うエネルギーショックや人工知能（ＡＩ）ブームの調整の可能性、世界的な債券利回り上昇の波及によるリスクが高まっていると警告した。

香港市場ではハンセン指数が１％下落し、ハンセンテック指数は２．７％安となった。アリババの香港上場株は３．７％下落。

ソウル株式市場は急落し、総合株価指数（ＫＯＳＰＩ）は約６カ月ぶりの安値で引けた。

米インフレ指標で根強い物価上昇圧力が示され追加利上げ観測が強まり、世界的に人工知能（ＡＩ）投資ブームへの疑念が強まる中で半導体株が急落した。

ＫＯＳＰＩは７．５７％安で終了し、終値として４月７日以来の安値を付けた。７営業日続落となり、連続下落日数は２０２４年９月以来の長さとなった。

取引時間中には一時９．２９％下落し、７月２９日以来となるサーキットブレーカーが発動され、取引が２０分間停止された。発動は２６年に入って１０回目、過去通算では１６回目となった。

レバレッジ型の単一銘柄上場投資信託（ＥＴＦ）の過熱を抑える政策措置を受け、７月以降落ち着きを取り戻していたボラティリティー指数は再び上昇し、８月下旬以来の高水準となった。

未来アセット証券のアナリスト、ソ・サンヨン氏は「市場は人工知能（ＡＩ）サービスにおける売上高の伸びそのものよりも、資金調達が持続可能かどうか、巨額のインフラ投資が実際の収益につながるかどうかに敏感に反応している」と述べた。

半導体大手サムスン電子は９．５％、同業ＳＫハイニックスは１１．１％、それぞれ下落した。前日の米国市場では、根強いインフレ懸念から追加利上げ観測が強まり、ＡＩ関連株が売られ、フィラデルフィア半導体指数が４．３％下落していた。

ＪＰモルガン（香港）で韓国株式戦略責任者を務めるミクソ・ダス氏は、サムスン電子とＳＫハイニックスの自社株買いが一巡し、市場は「新たな買い手を見つけるのに苦労している」と指摘。「６─１２カ月の時間軸では、これらのＡＩ関連銘柄はいずれも現在の水準を大幅に上回ると引き続き考えている」と述べた。

金融当局は市場動向を点検する緊急会合を開き、市場安定と投資家保護に向けて積極的に対応する方針を示した。

その他の主要銘柄も大半が下落し、電池メーカーのＬＧエナジーソリューションは４．６％安、現代自動車は５．７％安となった。取引された全９１７銘柄のうち、１１３銘柄が上昇、７８９銘柄が下落した。

海外投資家は３兆６０００億ウォン（２６億８０００万ドル）相当の売り越し。

シドニー株式市場は小幅続落して引けた。ただ、予想を下回る雇用統計を受けて利上げ観測が後退し、銀行株が買われたことで、世界的な株安による下げは限定的となった。

９月の豪雇用統計は就業者数が予想外に減少し、失業率は５年ぶり高水準の４．７％にとどまった。これを受けて利上げ観測が後退した。市場が織り込む１１月の利上げ確率は統計発表前の３２％から約１７％に、１２月利上げは５６％から２３％にそれぞれ低下した。

金利観測に敏感なオーストラリア３年債利回りは１カ月超ぶりの低水準の４．８００％に低下した。

銀行株が上昇し、金融株指数は２．２％高と８月中旬以降の高値で引けた。主力銘柄のコモンウェルス銀行は３．３％急伸した。

ショー・アンド・パートナーズのシニア投資アドバイザー、クレイグ・シドニー氏は「利上げ休止は住宅市場にプラスで、ローン返済負担が軽減され、ローン申請件数の増加、ひいては利益成長につながる可能性があるため、銀行株は大きく上昇した」と述べた。

世界的なリスク選好は後退した。米消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）の伸びが予想を上回り、年内の米連邦準備理事会（ＦＲＢ）の利上げ観測が強まったことで、アジアのハイテク株に売りが広がった。

世界的な株安で銅価格が下落したことを受け、鉱業株指数が４．３％超下落した。

ハイテク株指数は３．４％急落し、４月以来の安値で引けた。データセンター運営のネクストＤＣは７．４％安、マッコーリー・テクノロジーは８．９％安となった。

データセンターの不動産を手がけるグッドマン・グループは３．９％急落し、不動産指数は０．７％下落した。

item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ソウル株7.57％安で引け、半導体株急落で6カ月ぶり安値　取引停止発動 10/15 16:32 配信

10月15日、ソウルの銀行のトレーディングルームで撮影。 REUTERS/Kim Hong-Ji

[ソウル １５日 ロイター] - 韓国ソウル株式市場は急落し、総合株価指数（ＫＯＳＰＩ）は約６カ月ぶりの安値で引けた。

米インフレ指標で根強い物価上昇圧力が示され追加利上げ観測が強まり、世界的に人工知能（ＡＩ）投資ブームへの疑念が強まる中で半導体株が急落した。

ＫＯＳＰＩは４５４．５９ポイント（７．５７％）安の５５５４．２２で終了し、終値として４月７日以来の安値を付けた。７営業日続落となり、連続下落日数は２０２４年９月以来の長さとなった。

取引時間中には一時９．２９％下落し、７月２９日以来となるサーキットブレーカーが発動され、取引が２０分間停止された。発動は２６年に入って１０回目、過去通算では１６回目となった。

レバレッジ型の単一銘柄上場投資信託（ＥＴＦ）の過熱を抑える政策措置を受け、７月以降落ち着きを取り戻していたボラティリティー指数は再び上昇し、８月下旬以来の高水準となった。

未来アセット証券のアナリスト、ソ・サンヨン氏は「市場は人工知能（ＡＩ）サービスにおける売上高の伸びそのものよりも、資金調達が持続可能かどうか、巨額のインフラ投資が実際の収益につながるかどうかに敏感に反応している」と述べた。

半導体大手サムスン電子は９．５％、同業ＳＫハイニックスは１１．１％、それぞれ下落した。前日の米国市場では、根強いインフレ懸念から追加利上げ観測が強まり、ＡＩ関連株が売られ、フィラデルフィア半導体指数が４．３％下落していた。

ＪＰモルガン（香港）で韓国株式戦略責任者を務めるミクソ・ダス氏は、サムスン電子とＳＫハイニックスの自社株買いが一巡し、市場は「新たな買い手を見つけるのに苦労している」と指摘。「６─１２カ月の時間軸では、これらのＡＩ関連銘柄はいずれも現在の水準を大幅に上回ると引き続き考えている」と述べた。

金融当局は市場動向を点検する緊急会合を開き、市場安定と投資家保護に向けて積極的に対応する方針を示した。

その他の主要銘柄も大半が下落し、電池メーカーのＬＧエナジーソリューションは４．６％安、現代自動車は５．７％安となった。取引された全９１７銘柄のうち、１１３銘柄が上昇、７８９銘柄が下落した。

海外投資家は３兆６０００億ウォン（２６億８０００万ドル）相当の売り越し。

国内決済プラットフォームのウォン相場は１ドル＝１３４４．６ウォンと、前日終値の１３４２．３ウォンから０．１７％下落した。

最も流動性の高い３年物国債利回りは２．４ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）低下の３．８６１％、指標１０年物国債利回りは４．９ｂｐ低下の４．１９６％となった。

item.description: [東京 １５日 ロイター] - 髙島屋は１５日、２０２７年２月期の年間配当予想を従来の４０円から４４円に引き上げると...

item.content:encoded:
高島屋、27年2月期の配当予想引き上げ　通期純利益は据え置き 10/15 16:22 配信

都内の高島屋百貨店。2017年7月撮影。REUTERS/Issei Kato

[東京 １５日 ロイター] - 髙島屋は１５日、２０２７年２月期の年間配当予想を従来の４０円から４４円に引き上げると発表した。上期はインバウンド需要などを支えに国内外事業で計画を上回った。通期純利益予想は３８０億円で据え置いた。

・上期のインバウンド売上高は前年比１８％増の５１９億円と、リスクを考慮した当初計画（３％減の４２５億円）を大幅超過。円安や海外店舗からの送客などが奏功。

・上期の業績を踏まえ、通期の営業利益予想を従来の５７５億円から５９０億円に上方修正

・純利益は一過性の特別損失が発生するものの、政策保有株・不動産の資産売却益で吸収するとして据え置き

・配当は中間・期末ともに２円引き上げ

item.title: 午後3時のドルは157円後半で戻り鈍い、米金利に連動
item.description:
Kentaro Sugiyama
[東京 １５日 ロイター] -
ド...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
午後3時のドルは157円後半で戻り鈍い、米金利に連動 10/15 16:04 配信

米ドル紙幣。２０２３年３月撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic

Kentaro Sugiyama

[東京 １５日 ロイター] -

ドル／円 ユーロ／ドル ユーロ／円

午後３時現在 157.88／157.9 1.1215／1.1217 177.08／177.10

0

午前９時現在 157.97／158.0 1.1194／1.1195 176.85／176.86

0

ＮＹ午後５時 158.31／158.3 1.1156／1.1159 176.62／176.68

4

午後３時のドルは、前日ニューヨーク市場終盤に比べてドル安／円高の１５７円後半となっている。朝方は１５８円前半で推移していたが、米長期金利の低下に歩調を合わせてドル売りが優勢となり、一時１５７円半ばまで下落した。同水準では下げ渋ったものの、米金利の戻りが限られる中、朝方の水準を回復するには至らなかった。

前日海外時間は米消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）が市場予想を上回ったことを受けてドル買いが強まり、１５９円近辺まで上昇したが、その後は米金利が上昇幅を縮小し、ドル買いが一服した。

東京時間は米国市場での人工知能（ＡＩ）関連株の下落でＡＩ投資への懸念が浮上し、リスク回避ムードが強まった。米金利が低下し、ドルはほぼ全面安。日本と韓国での株安も投資家心理を冷やした。

午前に行われた日銀の小枝淳子審議委員のあいさつはタカ派的と受け止められ、為替市場では円高材料になったとの声も出ていた。

小枝委員は「物価上昇リスクが相応にあることを踏まえれば、利上げに過度に慎重になることはない」と述べたほか、中立金利水準は推計レンジ下限目安の１％より相応に上にあるとの考えを示した。

市場からは「コメント自体はタカ派的だが、日銀の利上げペースの一段の加速を意識させるようなものではない。小枝氏の説明全体のトーンは大きく変わっておらず、引き続き利上げ姿勢を示したという見方でよいのではないか」（ＳＭＢＣ日興証券の丸山凜途シニア金利・為替ストラテジスト）との声が聞かれた。

午後の記者会見で小枝氏は、今後の利上げについて「特定のペースを考えているわけではない」などと話した。

item.title: 日経平均は6日続落、一時5％超安 ＡＩ投資懸念で関連株急落
item.description:
Hiroko Hamada
[東京 １５日 ロイター] - 東京株式市場で日経平均は大幅に６日続落し、前営業日比４．９...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
日経平均は6日続落、一時5％超安　ＡＩ投資懸念で関連株急落 10/15 16:01 配信

東京証券取引所。２０２０年１０月、都内で撮影。REUTERS/Issei Kato

Hiroko Hamada

[東京 １５日 ロイター] - 東京株式市場で日経平均は大幅に６日続落し、前営業日比４．９０％（３３１８円３４銭）安の６万４４２５円９５銭で取引を終えた。下落幅は過去３番目の大きさとなった。前日の米市場でＡＩ（人工知能）投資懸念が強まり、東京市場でも関連銘柄が軒並み大幅安となった。日経平均は一時５％超安となる場面があった。一方、ディフェンシブ株には買いもみられたほか、決算を受けた個別物色は活発だった。

日経平均は前営業日比１．２８％安でスタートした後、徐々に下げ幅を拡大。後場には一時６万４０９２円７４銭まで値下がりした。前日の米市場では、ＡＩ向けクラウドサービスを提供するコアウィーブの株価が約１５％下落した。市場では、ＡＩインフラ投資が減速に向かう可能性が改めて意識された。加えて、９月の米消費者物価指数（ＣＰＩ）が市場予想を上振れたことも金利の先高観につながり、ハイテク株の重しとなった。日本株市場でも指数寄与度の大きい半導体関連株を中心に売りが加速した。一方、医薬品や小売など内需関連株は堅調に推移し、ディフェンシブ株には買いも入った。

後場終盤には台湾のＴＳＭＣ決算の内容が伝わったが、相場の反応は限定的だった。

松井証券のチーフマーケットアナリスト・窪田朋一郎氏は「米国ではデータセンター投資が持続するか懸念が強まっている。また、国内の半導体関連株は需給面で上値が重くなるとみられ、日経平均は２００日線が位置する６万１０００円近辺まで調整が深まる可能性もある」と指摘する。

目先は企業決算に投資家の関心が向かうが、「半導体関連企業では、足元の好業績は見込めるものの、先行きに対して企業側がどのようなメッセージを発信するか注目」（窪田氏）だという。

ＴＯＰＩＸは２．３８％安の３９９９．３４ポイントで取引を終えた。東証プライム市場指数は前営業日比２．３８％安の２０６１．３ポイントだった。プライム市場の売買代金は１０兆１４０１億２５００万円だった。東証３３業種では、医薬品、不動産、小売など１０業種が値上がり。非鉄金属、電機機器、ガラス・土石製品など２３業種は値下がりした。

新興株式市場は、東証グロース市場２５０指数が３日続落し、３．２１％安の７５６．５３ポイントだった。

個別では、ソフトバンクグループ、東京エレクトロン、アドバンテストが大幅下落し、３銘柄で日経平均を２０００円超押し下げた。キオクシアホールディングス、フジクラも大幅安。

一方、前日に決算を発表した良品計画は大幅高。同じく前日に決算とメニューの値上げを発表したサイゼリヤも大幅上昇した。

東証プライム市場の騰落数は、値上がりが５６４銘柄（３６％）、値下がりは９４８銘柄（６１％）、変わらずは４０銘柄（２％）だった。

item.title: 台湾総統、マイクロン労使に誠実な交渉要請 スト実施の可能性で
item.description:
Yi-Chin Lee Ann Wang
[台中 １５日 ロイター] - 米メモリー半導体大手マイクロン・テクノロジー...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
台湾総統、マイクロン労使に誠実な交渉要請　スト実施の可能性で 10/15 15:42 配信

マイクロン・テクノロジーの施設。９月、台湾の桃園市で撮影。REUTERS/Ann Wang

Yi-Chin Lee　Ann Wang

[台中 １５日 ロイター] - 米メモリー半導体大手マイクロン・テクノロジーの台湾の労働組合がストライキに踏み切る可能性があることを受け、頼清徳総統は１５日、労使双方に誠実な交渉を呼びかけた。

同労組は先週、賞与制度を巡る対立で、組合員からスト実施の承認を得たと発表した。同社は主要な製造拠点の一つである台湾で約１万５０００人を雇用している。

頼氏は台中で開かれたマイクロンの新たな先端組み立て・検査施設の開所式で、政府と民間が協力し、労使間の対話がさらに深まるよう後押しすることに期待を示した。

労使双方が誠意を持って交渉を続け、できる限り幅広い合意を築くことを望むとし、「調和の取れた労使関係を築いてこそ双方が利益を得られ、従業員が安心して働き、企業も着実に歩みを進め、さらに発展できる」と語った。

頼氏はマイクロンの台湾への取り組みに謝意を示し、投資を引き続き拡大することを期待していると述べた。また、同社が広帯域メモリー（ＨＢＭ）の研究開発で政府の支援を確保したと説明した。

マイクロンのマニシュ・バティア社長兼最高執行責任者（ＣＯＯ）は、頼氏に先立って行ったあいさつで、ストの可能性には言及しなかった。「この工場の２０２７年の生産能力に相当する分は、すでに全て売約済みだ。ＨＢＭは２８年まで一貫して、ＤＲＡＭの他の分野を上回るペースで成長すると見込んでいる」と述べた。

item.title: 利上げ「特定のペースは考えず」、会合ごとに判断＝小枝日銀委員
item.description:
Takahiko Wada
［熊本市 １５日 ロイター］ - 日銀の小枝淳子審議委員は１５日午後の記者会見で、今後の利...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
利上げ「特定のペースは考えず」、会合ごとに判断＝小枝日銀委員 10/15 15:36 配信

日本銀行本店。都内で２０２４年３月撮影。 REUTERS/Kim Kyung-Hoon

Takahiko Wada

［熊本市　１５日　ロイター］ - 日銀の小枝淳子審議委員は１５日午後の記者会見で、今後の利上げについて「特定のペースを考えているわけではない」と話した。９月に続き１０月の金融政策決定会合でも利上げを決める可能性があるのか問われたが、「その都度、経済・物価・金融環境を点検して判断していく」と述べるにとどめた。

午前の懇談会のあいさつでは、緩和的な金融環境が続くもとで、物価上昇リスクが「相応にある」ことを踏まえれば、利上げに「過度に慎重になることはない」と話していた。

９月会合は、６月から３カ月での追加利上げ決定となった。小枝委員は、金融緩和度合いの調節は「できる時にした方がいい」と話し、９月利上げに当たっては中東情勢の悪化を受けてもなお経済の底堅さが確認できたことが判断を後押ししたと説明した。

あいさつでは中立金利は「１％よりは相応に上」と述べていたが、会見ではそれ以上具体的な水準には言及しなかった。中立金利についてピンポイントで数値を言うことは難しく、「レンジを持って捉えていくことが必要」と強調した。

２％物価目標を「達成」しているのかとの質問には「安定性や持続性についてしっかり議論していく必要がある」と述べた。

小枝委員は、幅広い品目の物価上昇の持続と賃金の安定的な上昇を挙げた上で、基調的な物価上昇率が２％に「定着しつつある」とした。米国の高関税政策や中東情勢の悪化という「外部ショックを受けても、わが国経済は底堅さが見えている」と述べ、経済の底堅い推移も基調物価の定着度を上げる方向に作用していると説明した。

item.title: Ukraine hits Russian refinery as Zelenskiy says 'we're done' with Trump's energy truce
item.description: Ukraine struck a Russian oil refinery on Thursday, after President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said Kyiv was "done" supporting a ceasefire on energy targets announced by US President Donald Trump and ignored by Russia.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Flynn, Max Hunder
item.content:encoded: Ukraine struck a Russian oil refinery on Thursday, after President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said Kyiv was "done" supporting a ceasefire on energy targets announced by US President Donald Trump and ignored by Russia. Russian President Vladimir Putin [USN:L1N4610T1 TEXT:"played down"] the effect of Ukrainian long-range attacks on Russian refineries, saying they had caused "nothing particularly significant." Since Trump's surprise announcement on Sunday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to halt attacks on energy, Kyiv had suspended attacks on Russian refineries, which Trump blames for raising diesel prices on global markets. But in the days that followed, Russia rained down missile and drone strikes, including on energy targets such as power stations, knocking out power to hundreds of thousands of people. In an interview with the Financial Times published on Thursday, Zelenskiy said Ukraine's patience had run out. "The block (on attacking refineries) is out. We're done," he told the newspaper. Zelenskiy also criticised what he saw as Trump's willingness to strike deals with Russia, apparent admiration for Putin and an affinity for those wielding power or considerable wealth. "He (Trump) speaks about it openly and loudly that he loves such people and he respects such people," the FT quoted him as saying. "Because for him people who can be leaders 20 years, 30 years, 40 years, it means they can be very strong." Zelenskiy, who [USN:L1N46107Z TEXT:"was due to attend"] a European Union summit on Friday, also made clear he believed that changes in the capability of the military version of SpaceX's Starlink receptors this week, which have curbed Ukraine's ability to use them to pilot its drones, were a policy decision. "It was not a technical problem, it was the will," he told the FT. In a social media post overnight, SpaceX boss Elon Musk said usage of the military version of Starlink, known as Starshield, was ultimately up to Trump as president of the United States. "Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government. Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS," Musk wrote. BIGGEST RIFT WITH WASHINGTON OF THE WAR By effectively walking away from Trump's demand that Ukraine halt attacks on refineries, Zelenskiy risks deepening the biggest rift between Kyiv and Washington since Russia's invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Although Trump has described the ceasefire as a requirement for both Moscow and Kyiv, his public comments have focused mainly on Ukraine's attacks on Russian refineries, which he said over the weekend had "damn well better stop". Trump has long had a testy relationship with Zelenskiy and berated him in the White House in February 2025. But his sharp turn against Kyiv in recent days has little precedent. He first angered Ukraine last week by abruptly lifting sanctions on Russian diesel, and then called for Zelenskiy to be replaced. Ukrainians worry that the rift could have severe consequences on the battlefield, where the Ukrainian military still depends on technology provided by Washington. For several days, Ukrainian officials say they have not received the usual warnings from Western allies about incoming Russian missiles, which rely on US satellite detectors. Trump has denied withholding intelligence. At the same time, military-grade Starlink receptors have stopped working in Ukraine when mounted on fast-moving objects, interfering with the performance of Ukrainian drones that rely on them for onboard guidance systems over Ukrainian territory. A source in Ukraine's defence ministry said on Thursday that the receptors were now working when in motion, but only at speeds of up to 100 miles per hour (160 kph). Ukrainian officials say that is too slow for mid-range attack missions and interceptor drones that defend against Russian drones. Defence experts and a Reuters analysis of satellite imagery, meanwhile, [USN:L8N4601YV TEXT:"showed that"] Russia had in just six weeks nearly finished building a major base in southern Russia for launching jet-powered drones. REFINERY SUPPLYING MOSCOW HIT Ukraine has been using its long-range drones to target Russian refineries and logistics in recent months, which it says is its only answer to nearly five years of relentless Russian bombardment. The attacks have caused fuel shortages in Russia. Trump is under pressure, with his Republicans facing midterm elections in less than three weeks, to lower fuel prices. Prices for diesel have reached record highs since he launched a war against Iran in February, though Trump says the Ukrainian attacks are driving up global prices. Ukraine's latest target was a refinery in the Ryazan region southeast of Moscow, which is owned by state oil major Rosneft and accounts for nearly 5% of Russia's refinery throughput, helping supply the capital. Regional governor Pavel Malkov said on Telegram that a [USN:S8N44O03I TEXT:"major Ukrainian drone attack"] had caused a fire at the refinery. A Ukrainian official confirmed that Ukraine had hit a Russian refinery in response to Moscow's ballistic missile and drone attacks this week that violated the energy truce. In the Black Sea, rescuers searched for seven missing sailors after [USN:L8N4610EC TEXT:"drones struck"] two chemical tankers near Romania's Black Sea coast, setting them ablaze in the latest attack on shipping along a vital route used by Ukraine. Romanian President Nicusor Dan said the two ships had been struck by drones but declined to say whether Russia was responsible. A NATO source said the drones came from Russia. The Kremlin said on Thursday that Ukraine's targeting of Russian energy infrastructure ran counter to US peace efforts. It said earlier this week that the scope of the energy ceasefire had never been determined and work was ongoing to do so. BREAKDOWN IN RELATIONS Ukraine's rift with Washington has raised concern in Kyiv and European capitals about the heavy reliance in Ukraine on US intelligence and technology. Under Trump, Washington has already halted weapons supplies to Ukraine while allowing its European allies to continue buying US arms on Kyiv's behalf. But [USN:L6N460199 TEXT:"Europe has no ready-made alternatives"] to Starlink, or to US satellite systems used to detect Russian missile launches. Zelenskiy has said that Ukrainian military officials had been warned by US counterparts that Washington would block intelligence unless they halted strikes on Russian energy infrastructure. Asked whether Ukraine would be open to halting energy strikes as a way of repairing relations with the White House, Zelenskiy told the FT he could agree only if in return he were given more US-made Patriot interceptors as a "minimum".

item.title: ＴＳＭＣ第3四半期、純利益69％増で最高益 27年は慎重姿勢
item.description:
Wen-Yee Lee Ben Blanchard
[台北 １５日 ロイター] - 半導体受託生産世界最大手の台湾積体...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＴＳＭＣ第3四半期、純利益69％増で最高益　27年は慎重姿勢 10/15 14:58 配信

台湾積体電路製造（ＴＳＭＣ）のロゴ。７月、台湾の台北で撮影。REUTERS/Ann Wang

Wen-Yee Lee　Ben Blanchard

[台北 １５日 ロイター] - 半導体受託生産世界最大手の台湾積体電路製造（ＴＳＭＣ）が１５日発表した第３・四半期（７─９月）決算は、テクノロジーセクターのインフラ投資急増に支えられて１１四半期連続の増益となり、６四半期連続で過去最高益を記録した。需要は「極めて旺盛」とし、人工知能（ＡＩ）の「メガトレンド」に減速の兆しはないと、強気の見通しを示したものの、マクロ経済の不確実性を理由に２０２７年については慎重な姿勢を示した。

第３・四半期の純利益は前年同期比６９％増の７６３１億台湾ドル（２３５億９０００万米ドル）で、ＬＳＥＧスマートエスティメートによるアナリスト１６人の予想７４６３億台湾ドルを上回った。８日に発表した売上高は５０％増の１兆４９００億台湾ドルで過去最高だった。

エヌビディアやアップルなどを顧客に持つＴＳＭＣは、需要が供給能力を大幅に上回っていると説明し、２６年通期売上高は約４４％増加と、従来予想（４０％超増加）から引き上げた。エージェント型ＡＩ向け中央演算処理装置（ＣＰＵ）の登場やネットワーク用半導体への継続的な需要が、今後の半導体需要をけん引するとの見方も示した。２６年の設備投資計画は６００億─６４０億米ドルで据え置いた。

魏哲家最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は決算説明会で「部品価格の上昇とマクロ経済の不確実性により、消費者向けや価格変動の影響を受けやすい最終製品市場は引き続き厳しい状況にある」とし、「このため、２７年に向けた事業計画は慎重に策定している」と述べた。

ＴＳＭＣ株を保有するオールスプリング・グローバル・インベストメンツのポートフォリオマネジャー、ゲーリー・タン氏は、同社の発言は多くの半導体企業が最近の決算発表や投資家向け説明会で示した慎重姿勢を反映したものだと指摘した。「主なリスクは、ＴＳＭＣの慎重姿勢が、業績予想の上方修正が続くことに慣れたバリューチェーン全体で、幅広い下方修正につながることだ。ただ現時点では、セクターの長期的なファンダメンタルズ（基礎的条件）の変化というより、賢明な期待値の管理のように見える」と述べた。

アナリストによると、ＴＳＭＣのＡＩ半導体の生産能力や、先端パッケージング技術「ＣｏＷｏＳ」に対する需要は引き続き旺盛だ。

＜米生産能力拡大　テキサス州で評価作業＞

ＴＳＭＣは米アリゾナ州での半導体工場建設に２６５０億ドルを投じる計画だ。

同州では第２工場の建設が完了し、量産開始は２７年第３・四半期を予定しているという。

ロイターは９月、ＴＳＭＣが米国での生産拡大に向けテキサス州への追加投資を検討していると報じた。

魏氏は、米国の主要顧客から現地生産能力の拡大を求められており、アリゾナ州以外での拡張の可能性を検討していると説明した。米政府も支援してくれているという。「テキサス州はその一つだ。チームをテキサス州に派遣し、あらゆる評価を行った」と述べた。

米テスラのイーロン・マスクＣＥＯは７日、自身が率いる企業がＡＩ半導体の複合施設「テラファブ」を建設・運営し、ＴＳＭＣがその一部をサブリース（転貸借）する可能性があると述べた。魏氏は、テラファブと協議したことを認めた上で、工場で協業する場合はＴＳＭＣが運営しなければならないと述べた。

item.title: ＡＩ関連企業のＣＤＳ保証料率が過去最高、巨額投資や債務への不安高まる
item.description: ［シンガポール １５日 ロイター］ - 米テック企業のデフォルト（債務不履行）に備える保証コストが過去最高の水準に達...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
ＡＩ関連企業のＣＤＳ保証料率が過去最高、巨額投資や債務への不安高まる 10/15 14:55 配信

ＡＩ（人工知能）の文字。６月、フランスのパリで開催された第１０回ビバテックで撮影。REUTERS/Gonzalo Fuentes

［シンガポール　１５日　ロイター］ -  米テック企業のデフォルト（債務不履行）に備える保証コストが過去最高の水準に達した。人工知能（ＡＩ）関連の取引で信用不安が、データセンター事業者を中心に強まっている。ＡＩへの巨額投資がどれだけ早く利益につながるのか、また多額の債務を抱える企業が膨らむ利払い費を賄えるだけの収益を上げられるようになるのかが懸念されている。

Ｓ＆Ｐグローバル・マーケット・インテリジェンスによると、クラウドコンピューティング大手オラクルの５年物クレジット・デフォルト・スワップ（ＣＤＳ）スプレッドは２６ベーシスポイント（ｂｐ）拡大し、過去最高の２８８ｂｐとなった。

ＡＩ分野に投資するソフトバンクグループも２４ｂｐ拡大し、４２４ｂｐとなった。ＬＳＥＧのデータによると、データセンター運営コアウィーブは１０００ｂｐを突破した。

コアウィーブは業績が赤字で、ＬＳＥＧのデータによると５００億ドル近い債務を抱える。株価は１４日に１５％下落し、時間外取引でさらに６％下げた。時価総額の５分の１が吹き飛んだ。社債価格も急落し、２０３２年償還債は額面１ドル当たり０．７７ドルで取引されている。

ＬＳＥＧとＳ＆Ｐグローバル・マーケット・インテリジェンスのデータによると、アマゾン・ドット・コム、アルファベット、メタ・プラットフォームズ、エヌビディアのＣＤＳスプレッドも、水準的にはオラクルを大幅に下回るが過去最大に広がった。

item.title: 独政府、欧州防衛大手ＫＮＤＳ株の50％取得に向け協議中＝関係筋
item.description: [ベルリン １４日 ロイター] - ドイツ政府は、ドイツ・フランス系防衛大手ＫＮＤＳのドイツ側オーナー一族から同社株式...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
独政府、欧州防衛大手ＫＮＤＳ株の50％取得に向け協議中＝関係筋 10/15 14:45 配信

写真は戦車「レオパルト２」。７月、ドイツ・カッセルのＫＮＤＳで撮影。REUTERS/Fabian Bimmer

[ベルリン １４日 ロイター] - ドイツ政府は、ドイツ・フランス系防衛大手ＫＮＤＳのドイツ側オーナー一族から同社株式の５０％を取得する交渉を進めている。事情に詳しい関係者が明らかにした。今年に入り、同社の新規株式公開（ＩＰＯ）を巡る市場環境が悪化していることが背景にある。

関係者がロイターに語ったところによると、ドイツ側一族との交渉は現在も続いており、取得価格を巡る双方の隔たりはそれほど大きくないという。

ドイツ経済紙ハンデルスブラットは１４日、数週間以内に決定が下される見通しだと報じた。

この関係者と別の関係者はロイターに対し、ＫＮＤＳのＩＰＯ計画は保留となっていると語った。ＫＮＤＳの上場は、近年の欧州防衛セクターにおける最大規模のＩＰＯとなるはずだった。

当初の計画では、ＫＮＤＳ株式を５０％ずつ保有するドイツ側一族とフランス政府が、それぞれ１０％の株式を投資家に売却し、一族が保有する残りの４０％はドイツ政府に売却される予定だった。

ドイツ経済省は１４日、重要な防衛産業技術を保護するため、フランスと同等の条件で株式を取得することを政府が検討していると明らかにした。同省報道官は電子メールの声明で「株式の売買に関する決定権は株主に帰属する」と述べた。

item.title: 米大手行、金利急騰で債券部門苦戦 株式取引は好調
item.description:
Tatiana Bautzer
[ニューヨーク １４日 ロイター] - このほど発表された米大手銀行の第３・四半期決算...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
米大手行、金利急騰で債券部門苦戦　株式取引は好調 10/15 14:35 配信

ニューヨーク証券取引所（ＮＹＳＥ）のロゴ。９月、米ニューヨーク市で撮影。REUTERS/Jeenah Moon

Tatiana Bautzer

[ニューヨーク １４日 ロイター] - このほど発表された米大手銀行の第３・四半期決算には、債券価格急落（利回り急騰）の影響が色濃く表れた。金利変動の高まりを受けて顧客との取引が鈍り、多くの銀行で債券・為替・商品（ＦＩＣＣ）部門の収益が前年同期比で減少した。

第３・四半期には米国債利回りが数十年ぶりの高水準に達し、投資家が金利見通しを見直す中で、市場では急激な価格変動が発生。米長期金利の指標となる１０年国債利回りは９月末時点で、２００９年以来最大の四半期上昇を記録した。

モルガン・スタンレーのＦＩＣＣ収益は前年同期比７％減少。ＪＰモルガン・チェースは４％減、バンク・オブ・アメリカは１７％減だった。一方、ゴールドマン・サックスは横ばいを維持し、シティグループは４％増収と主要行の中で唯一のプラスだった。

モルガン・スタンレーのシャロン・イェシャヤ最高財務責任者（ＣＦＯ）は「金利は第３・四半期を通じて予想以上のペースで上昇した」と指摘。仕組み取引への需要が低下したほか、信用スプレッドの拡大が債券保有投資家にとって重荷になったと説明した。

バンク・オブ・アメリカのアラステア・ボースウィックＣＦＯは「顧客活動の減少と、金利の大幅な変動を含む市場環境の変化が、クレジット、モーゲージ、地方債を含むＦＩＣＣ事業に大きな影響を与えた」と述べた。

シティグループでは、ＦＩＣＣ収益の４％増の大半を外国為替取引とスプレッド商品が占めた。ジェーン・フレーザー最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）はアナリスト向け説明会で「金利関連収益は市場環境の影響を受けたが、為替取引とスプレッド商品は伸びた」と解説した。

一方、長期金利上昇は各行のバランスシートにも影響を与え、有価証券ポートフォリオの含み損が拡大した。

バンク・オブ・アメリカが保有する住宅ローン担保証券（ＭＢＳ）や米国債、政府機関債などの債券ポートフォリオの含み損は９月末時点で１０９０億ドルとなり、６月末の８５０億ドルから増加した。これらの証券の大半は満期保有（ＨＴＭ）区分に計上されており、同行は売却を予定していない。

大手行の株式取引部門は大幅な増収になった。ゴールドマン・サックスの株式取引収益はデリバティブ取引とファイナンシング業務の拡大を背景に前年同期比７２％増加。モルガン・スタンレーは４１％増、ＪＰモルガンは４９％増だった。

バンク・オブ・アメリカとシティグループもそれぞれ１１％増、１４％増と伸びたものの、主要行の中では比較的小幅な増加にとどまった。

オッペンハイマーのアナリスト、クリス・コトウスキー氏は、株式取引収益への依存度上昇について「収益の変動リスクが高まる可能性がある。こうした収益には『得やすい一方で失いやすい』側面がある」と顧客向けリポートで警鐘を鳴らした。

ロイター 関連ニュース アングル：米大手銀、ＡＩブームの波に乗る一方で警戒も　収益機会とリスクが併存 アングル：ＡＩ関連の資金調達、低格付け領域にも拡大　投資家は警戒感強める コラム：ベセント氏の危うい賭け、ＡＩ主導の経済成長は「債務病」の特効薬ならず コラム：進む米中デカップリング、中国「保有米国債」の脅威減退か コラム：トランプ米大統領、任期中の利下げは望み薄　市場は高金利長期化を想定 最終更新: 10/15(木) 14:35 ロイター

item.title: Gold rebounds on weaker dollar, yield drop; October Fed hike bets subdued
item.description: Gold climbed more than 1% on Thursday, looking set to snap three sessions of losses, supported by a weaker dollar and lower US Treasury yields, while expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike this month remained subdued despite hotter-than-expected inflation data.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Sinha
item.content:encoded: Gold climbed more than 1% on Thursday, looking set to snap three sessions of losses, supported by a weaker dollar and lower US Treasury yields, while expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike this month remained subdued despite hotter-than-expected inflation data. Spot gold was up 1.2% at $4,153.42 per ounce by 2:01 p.m. EDT (1801 GMT), after slipping to a one-week low in the previous session. US gold futures for December delivery settled 1.5% higher at $4,170.10 per ounce. The dollar (.DXY) slipped 0.5%, while the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield was at a three-week low. "I think the market was largely anticipating the hot PPI print in the wake of yesterday's higher than expected CPI number," said Peter Grant, vice president and senior metals strategist at Zaner Metals. "The market is starting to realize that the Fed is hamstrung to some degree because of the fiscal situation and that raising interest rates much higher is going to be quite a burden to the economy." Higher interest rates make the non-yielding asset less attractive. US [USN:L1N460127 TEXT:"producer prices increased"] by the most in 4-1/2 years in September amid rising costs for goods and services, the latest indication of inflation broadening out beyond energy products. The data followed Wednesday's consumer price report, which showed [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"prices"] accelerated in September on a surge in gasoline costs. Market pricing for an October Fed rate hike rose sharply after the CPI data. However, San Francisco Fed President [USN:L6N4601E8 TEXT:"Mary Daly"] and Vice Chair for Supervision [USN:L1N4600EO TEXT:"Michelle Bowman"] said an immediate rate hike might not be required, tempering expectations of an October rate hike. Traders are now pricing in about a 29% chance of a rate hike later this month, according to CME's FedWatch Tool . Investors are also looking out for Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's comments at the International Monetary Fund's annual meeting at 11:30 p.m. EDT for any clues ahead of this month's Fed meeting. Among other metals, spot silver gained 2.5% to $57.05 per ounce, platinum rose 1% to $1,622.40 per ounce and palladium climbed 3.4% to $1,131.25 per ounce.

item.title: Comedian Russell Brand was a ruthless sexual predator, UK prosecutors say
item.description: British comedian Russell Brand faces 7 charges involving rape, sexual assault and indecent assault against 6 women. He denies all allegations concerning incidents between 1999 and 2009.
item.dc:creator: CNA Lifestyle
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

Entertainment

Comedian Russell Brand was a ruthless sexual predator, UK prosecutors say

British comedian Russell Brand faces 7 charges involving rape, sexual assault and indecent assault against 6 women. He denies all allegations concerning incidents between 1999 and 2009.

British actor and comedian Russell Brand arrives at Southwark Crown Court where he stands trial on charges of rape and sexual assault involving six women between 1999 and 2009, which he denies, in London, Britain, October 14, 2026. REUTERS/Jack Taylor

15 Oct 2026 10:08AM

Bookmark

Bookmark

Get bite-sized news via a new cards interface. Give it a try.

Click here to return to FAST Tap here to return to FAST

FAST

Actor and comedian Russell Brand, once one of Britain's most high-profile broadcasters, was a ruthless predator who raped or abused six women to satisfy his voracious sexual appetite, prosecutors said on Wednesday (Oct 14). Brand, 51, the former husband of US singer Katy Perry, is on trial facing three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one count of indecent assault relating to six women from 1999 to 2009. He denies all the accusations and will set out his defence in court at a later date. "Today I feel blessed," he said as he arrived at London's Southwark Crown Court. "I feel of course concerned but hopeful that this process will lead to good outcomes for everybody involved." DESIRE WAS INDISCRIMINATE, PROSECUTOR TELLS COURT

Russell Brand speaks to the media as he arrives at Southwark Crown Court in London, Wednesday Oct. 14, 2026. (Ben Whitley/PA via AP)

Prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones said some of the six women had protested, while others had no opportunity to react to his advances. It had made no difference to Brand, she said. "His desire, his strong desire, for some form of sexual contact was indiscriminate and voracious," she said. Although he could be funny and charming when he wanted something, he also had a childlike expectation his every desire should be met, she added. "He was ruthless, he was calculating, he was manipulative and, the prosecution say, he was a sexual predator," Karmy-Jones said. The alleged offences took place over a decade as Brand progressed from gigs as a stand-up comedian to a TV presenter, actor and Hollywood movie star. FIRST ALLEGED OFFENCE IN 1999

British actor and comedian Russell Brand appears at Southwark Crown Court where he stands trial on charges of rape and sexual assault involving six women between 1999 and 2009, which he denies, in London, Britain, October 14, 2026, in this courtroom sketch. REUTERS/Julia Quenzler

The first is alleged to have occurred in 1999 when he was performing in a show on the fringe of the Labour Party Conference in Bournemouth. The first complainant, who had watched the show and had assumed Brand was gay, said he had raped her in her hotel room where she had invited him to talk. Mark Pinheiro, one of his co-performers at the show who Brand went on to live with for about a year, said Brand bragged that he had wanted to bed 5,000 women in his lifetime. Giving evidence, Pinheiro said on their last morning in Bournemouth, Brand had returned to where they were staying looking flustered and told them they had to immediately leave. Pinheiro said that, a couple of months later, Brand admitted he had met a woman the night before and things "may have gone a little bit too far". Brand's lawyer Ian Winter suggested to Pinheiro that he did not mention that when he first contacted police and no such conversation took place, which Pinheiro rejected. BRAND SAYS HE NEVER ENGAGED IN NON-CONSENSUAL ACTIVITY

Russell Brand speaks to the media as he arrives at Southwark Crown Court in London, Wednesday Oct. 14, 2026. (Ben Whitley/PA via AP)

The second charge relates to 2001, when he is accused of trying to drag a woman into a toilet cubicle at MTV Europe where she worked. Three years later, a woman said he had dragged her into a toilet cubicle in a bar before orally raping her. Around the same time in 2004 or 2005, a woman working at a media company said he indecently assaulted her. The fifth complainant, a fan, had consensual sex at his home in 2009 but then he anally raped her, the prosecutor said. The sixth, who worked for Channel 4, alleges Brand had demanded a massage and then pressed his face into her groin, also in 2009. When interviewed by police, Brand declined to answer questions but provided written statements in which he said he did not remember the incidents and had never engaged in non-consensual activity, Karmy-Jones said. WOMEN CAME FORWARD AFTER TV PROGRAMME The women involved did not know each other and did not contact the police until after a TV programme and a press report in 2023 in which anonymous allegations were made by other women, the prosecutor said. Brand sat in the dock wearing a dark suit and thin, white scarf, staring forward intently. His trial, expected to last about six weeks, has attracted huge media attention. The comedian, known for his flamboyant style and appearance, became famous in Britain before starring in a number of films including "Get Him to the Greek" in 2010, the same year he married Perry. They divorced in 2012. More recently Brand has appeared in online broadcasts discussing US politics, religion and free speech.

Source: Reuters/mm

item.title: Dollar recedes from 18-month high as bond rally tempers impact of hot inflation data
item.description: The dollar retreated from an 18-month peak on Thursday as investors looked past strong US inflation and spending data to focus on a shakeout in the securities of AI data center firms.
item.dc:creator: Laura Matthews
item.content:encoded: The dollar retreated from an 18-month peak on Thursday as investors looked past strong US inflation and spending data to focus on a shakeout in the securities of AI data center firms. US producer prices rose by the most in 4-1/2 years in September as goods and services costs increased, adding to evidence that inflation pressures are spreading beyond energy. Retail sales [USN:L1N460114 TEXT:"rose more than expected"] last month, lifted by higher gasoline prices, while weekly jobless claims [USN:L1N4600ZS TEXT:"marginally increased"], pointing to resilient consumer demand and a stable labor market. But government bonds rallied and the dollar pulled back, reflecting cautious remarks from Federal Reserve officials that further cooled expectations for an October interest-rate hike. "We have a narrative that is dollar negative based on the idea that inflation at this level and this quick pace is unsustainable," said Juan Perez, director of trading at Monex USA in Washington. "Regardless of no good news on the war front or the equity picture looking pessimistic, the market is anti-USD after a heavy dose of strengthening in the last four weeks. ... The economic stagnation seems to be having more influence in (the) mind of traders." AI COMPANIES' DEBT BURDENS The dollar index , which measures the US currency against a basket of peers, fell 0.45% to 101.99, having hit an 18-month high on Wednesday after US inflation figures came in stronger than expected. That helped the euro bounce 0.56% from an 18-month trough to $1.1218, putting it on track for its biggest daily gain in nearly two months. Sterling strengthened 0.64% to $1.3275 after data showed [USN:L8N4610AT TEXT:"Britain's economy unexpectedly grew"] 0.1% in August. Markets [USN:L6N46100A TEXT:"grew choppy"] after Wednesday's [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"hot US CPI reading"] initially bolstered bets on higher-for-longer Fed rates, while renewed concerns over AI companies' heavy debt burdens fuelled safe-haven flows into Treasuries. "The selloff in chip stocks offers support to bonds, helping keep yields in check despite the inflationary signals," said Uto Shinohara, senior investment strategist at Mesirow Currency Management. Traders now see a 73% chance that the Fed will leave rates unchanged at its October 27-28 meeting, compared with 53% a month ago, CME Group's FedWatch Tool showed. The expected likelihood of a hike [USN:L6N4600VL TEXT:"rose sharply"] after the CPI report, but bets eased after Fed officials including Vice Chair for Supervision [USN:L1N4600EO TEXT:"Michelle Bowman"] and San Francisco Fed President [USN:L6N4601E8 TEXT:"Mary Daly"] said the central bank could wait for more clarity before the meeting. "If yields struggle to extend higher and dollar rallies continue to attract sellers, it will strengthen our conviction that the inflation news is largely absorbed, leaving the balance of risks tilted in favor of risk assets," said Joel Kruger, a market strategist at LMAX Group in London. Investors will also watch remarks from Fed officials including Chair Kevin Warsh at IMF-World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok on Friday for clues on the US central bank's next move. The Australian dollar weakened 0.77% to $0.6919, after [USN:L1N46100L TEXT:"local employment"] unexpectedly slid in September, while the Japanese yen strengthened 0.15% to 158.08 per dollar. "With the Fed entering its blackout period shortly and no tier-one data releases remaining before the meeting, market direction will likely remain driven by geopolitical uncertainty surrounding Russia/Ukraine and Iran, alongside developments in the AI story," said Shinohara.

item.title: Brent steady as US weighs easing sanctions on global 'shadow fleet'
item.description: Brent crude was little changed on Thursday as investors weighed possible US steps to ease restrictions on the world’s "shadow fleet" of tankers, while conflict in the Middle East kept a geopolitical risk premium in the market.
item.dc:creator: Georgina Mccartney
item.content:encoded: Brent crude was little changed on Thursday as investors weighed possible US steps to ease restrictions on the world’s "shadow fleet" of tankers, while conflict in the Middle East kept a geopolitical risk premium in the market. The international benchmark settled down 14 cents, or 0.13%, at $105.92 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate crude futures settled up $2.88, or 3.03%, to $97.97 a barrel, after a large US crude stock draw helped support prices. The shadow fleet discussions are happening days after President Donald Trump [USN:L4N45Y0AR TEXT:"temporarily lifted sanctions"] on Russian diesel fuel to ease a surge in prices globally. The new talks centre on Washington potentially allowing "legal oil" to flow on previously sanctioned vessels, [USN:L1N46017R TEXT:"a US official said"]. The Department of Energy said any move to relieve sanctions on the shadow fleet would not help [USN:L1N46017R TEXT:"Russia "]move oil or oil products. The Treasury Department referred questions to the Department of Energy. US crude stocks and distillate inventories fell while gasoline inventories rose last week, the Energy Information Administration said on Thursday. Crude inventories fell by 8.6 million barrels to 415.6 million barrels in the week ended October 9, the EIA said, compared with analysts' expectations in a Reuters poll for a 288,000-barrel draw. SHIP ATTACKS SUSTAIN OIL RISK PREMIUM Escalating conflict between Saudi Arabia and Yemen's Houthis and renewed attacks on ships in the region supported prices. A [USN:L1N4600JW TEXT:"container ship and a dry bulk carrier both sank"] near the Strait of Hormuz after being hit by projectiles in separate incidents, maritime officials said on Wednesday. Attacks around the waterway have surged over the past 10 days, with Iran saying it was stepping up strikes in response to the US blockade of its ports and tougher sanctions introduced last month. "The ongoing conflict between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis is keeping a geopolitical premium in oil markets, but energy infrastructure has not been attacked in the last several days," MUFG analysts said in a note. Houthis fired missiles at the [USN:L1N4610QE TEXT:"presidential palace complex "]in the southern city of Aden on Thursday, killing two guards, while the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen detailed dozens of attacks on Saudi infrastructure in the escalating conflict. [USN:L6N4610BB TEXT:"Ukraine resumed its attacks"] on Russian refineries with a strike on a plant in the Ryazan region, after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy voiced anger at a "dangerous" withdrawal of US intelligence. The International Energy Agency [USN:L1N4610MY TEXT:"agreed "]on Thursday to release over 20 million barrels of diesel to the market as soon as possible and any oil remaining from a record emergency reserves release pledged in March to boost supply and cool soaring prices. In March, countries had pledged to release more than 400 million barrels of crude and oil products as prices soared. Spain will [USN:L6N4610OA TEXT:"release"] 4.4 million barrels from strategic reserves in October, an Energy Ministry official said on Thursday.

item.title: Global stocks flat as AI and rate fears hit tech
item.description: Global equity markets were flat on Thursday as concerns about AI spending and higher interest rates fueled a continued selloff in technology and chip stocks.
item.dc:creator: Chibuike Oguh
item.content:encoded: Global equity markets were flat on Thursday as concerns about AI spending and higher interest rates fueled a continued selloff in technology and chip stocks. Investors have been unnerved by valuations of companies in the AI ecosystem as more voices question the sustainability of demand for data centers. On Wall Street, the Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index (.SOX) was last down 1.7%. The benchmark S&P 500 and the Nasdaq reversed losses in early trade and were trading higher, led by healthcare and materials stocks, while the Dow was up 1%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI) rose 1.08%, the S&P 500 (.SPX) rose 0.27%, and the Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) rose 0.11%. "There's definitely a lot of investor skittishness right now about the path forward for AI," said Amanda Agati, chief investment officer at PNC Financial Services Group. A brutal tech-led selloff had hit stocks in Asia. South Korea's KOSPI index (.KS11) , whose flock of top chipmakers made it one of the main beneficiaries of AI euphoria, plunged almost 8%, while the Nikkei 225 (.N225) fell nearly 5%. "I think the selloff reflects investor caution towards the more vulnerable segment of the AI ecosystem, with tech chiefs advocating a slower pace of frontier model development," said Rong Ren Goh, portfolio manager at Eastspring Investments. "Markets increasingly question the sustainability and trajectory of demand for computing capacity. These concerns are compounded by higher funding costs, which raise the investment hurdle rates of capital-intensive AI infrastructure projects." MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan (.MISX00000PUS) closed 3.12% lower, marking its biggest one-day drop since late July. MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe (.MIWD00000PUS) fell 0.01%. European stocks (.STOXX) erased early-session losses and finished up 0.38%. BOND YIELDS FALL Benchmark 10-year US Treasury yields fell back towards 5% in what was their biggest daily drop in more than a year. US producer prices rose by the most in 4-1/2 years in September as goods and services costs increased, suggesting that inflation pressures are spreading beyond energy. New US [USN:L1N460114 TEXT:"retail sales data"] showed they increased more than expected last month, boosted by higher gasoline prices, but they also pointed to spending elsewhere remaining moderate. The yield on benchmark US 10-year notes fell 10.29 basis points to 5.087%. DOLLAR DROPS Wednesday's [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"US inflation data"] had once again tweaked expectations for the Fed's rate path, with traders briefly pricing in roughly even odds of a hike this month, before scaling back those bets. Fed funds futures are now pricing an implied 73% probability the US central bank will stay on hold at the end of its next two-day meeting on October 28, little changed from the start of the week, according to the CME Group's FedWatch tool. In the currency markets, the dollar slipped from an 18-month peak. Against the yen it was down 0.09% at 158.15 yen, while the euro was up 0.47% at $1.12 and sterling was 0.57% higher and buying $1.33. In [USN:L1N46101K TEXT:"oil markets"], Brent crude fell 0.13% to settle at $105.92 a barrel as traders weighed up the effects of US sanctions relief on supply against attacks on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Spot gold rose 1.38% to $4,161.82 an ounce.

item.title: US considers removing sanctions on some shadow fleet vessels to cut freight rates, official says
item.description: The Trump administration is considering lifting sanctions on some so-called shadow fleet vessels that have transported oil and petroleum products from countries including Russia, Iran and Venezuela, in an effort to reduce record-high global freight rates, a US official said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Timothy Gardner, Jarrett Renshaw
item.content:encoded: The Trump administration is considering lifting sanctions on some so-called shadow fleet vessels that have transported oil and petroleum products from countries including Russia, Iran and Venezuela, in an effort to reduce record-high global freight rates, a US official said on Wednesday. The discussions come days after President Donald Trump temporarily [USN:S0N43U024 TEXT:"lifted sanctions"] on Russian diesel fuel, a move met with a torrent of criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy, [USN:S8N43U03J TEXT:"European"] countries and some of Trump's [USN:L1N45Z0TJ TEXT:"fellow Republicans"] in the US Senate. Both Zelenskiy and the US senators called that move a gift to Russian President Vladimir Putin that would provide Russia with revenue to keep funding its war in Ukraine. The new talks center on the United States potentially allowing "legal oil" to flow on previously sanctioned vessels, the US official said. That means crude or petroleum products not sanctioned by Washington rather than Russian and Iranian oil, which are under punitive measures. The goal is to move more refined products and crude out of the Gulf, the official said. Companies seeking to buy the sanctioned vessels would have to apply to the US Treasury Department for approval of the transactions, the official said. A Treasury Department official told Reuters that the agency undertakes a "thorough review before removing sanctions on any entity." If legitimate buyers want to purchase the vessels and restore them for use by global commercial shipping, Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control "may consider authorizing those transactions and removing sanctions on those vessels on a case-by-case basis," the official said. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said in a video to the World Petroleum Congress in Riyadh this week that the administration was discussing easing sanctions on shadow fleet vessels in an effort to lower record freight rates that have hurt demand for US crude, according to Energy Aspects, a research group. Portions of the remarks were broadcast on social media, but Reuters was not able to obtain the full video or a transcript. The Department of Energy said it was not available. The Department of Energy said any move to relieve sanctions on the shadow fleet would not help Russia move oil or oil products. But Trump's push to move Russian diesel to global markets quickly could put pressure on the departments to allow shipment via the vessels. The White House did not respond immediately to a request for comment. High oil and fuel prices are a risk for Trump in the November 3 midterm elections in which Republicans are hoping to maintain control of both chambers of Congress. He lifted the sanctions on Russian diesel through April 7. RECORD HIGHS Tanker freight rates have [USN:L4N45U0OZ TEXT:"soared to record highs"] as the wars in Iran and Ukraine have stoked inflation and put US crude oil out of reach for Asian refiners, pushing them to seek alternatives from the Middle East and Latin America. Energy Aspects said in a note to clients that easing the sanctions on the shadow fleet would not greatly impact freight rates but could allow more movement of oil in the Middle East. Lifting the sanctions on the tankers, which are mostly old and not well maintained, is "unlikely to add meaningful mainstream fleet capacity overnight, especially as most tankers sanctioned over Russian or Venezuelan links have been actively trading over the past three months," it said in the note. Easing the restrictions "could make a small number of additional tankers available for certain (Strait of) Hormuz shuttle runs," in the waterway between Iran and Oman. Lifting the measures is unlikely to result in a broad easing of freight rates as ship insurers will still be bound by EU and UK regulations, maritime industry sources said.

item.title: Costa Rica opens mega-prison as organized crime fight intensifies
item.description: Costa Rica inaugurated a maximum-security prison on Wednesday as it stepped up its fight against organized crime after a surge in killings in what was long one of Latin America's safest countries.
item.dc:creator: Alvaro Murillo
item.content:encoded: Costa Rica inaugurated a maximum-security prison on Wednesday as it stepped up its fight against organized crime after a surge in killings in what was long one of Latin America's safest countries. President Laura Fernandez opened the High-Containment Center Against Organized Crime, or CACCO, a prison modeled on El Salvador's mega-prison and a key element of Salvadoran President Nayib Bukele's [USN:L6N41418X TEXT:"anti-gang crackdown"]. The facility near the capital of San Jose has a capacity for 5,100 inmates, roughly 20% of the nation's current prison population. Costa Rica recorded an all-time high of 905 homicides in 2023, according to judicial data. Killings eased only slightly to 876 in 2024 and 873 in 2025, remaining well above earlier levels. Authorities have said most murders are linked to disputes among criminal groups over drug trafficking routes and local markets. "The CACCO will force criminals to face a new model—a tough-on-crime model. Costa Rica will become a global benchmark for prison security," Fernandez said during the inauguration ceremony. The president also announced a visit to El Salvador on Friday. Bukele's crackdown is widely credited with sharply reducing gang violence in El Salvador, but rights groups say it has also brought [USN:L5N2X55DT TEXT:"mass arbitrary detentions"], due process violations and an [USN:L1N3ST0XG TEXT:"erosion of democratic safeguards"]. Fernandez said the new prison's impact would depend in part on the judiciary securing more convictions. Her government has clashed with judicial authorities over crime policy and budget cuts, while judges and prosecutors have warned against pressure on democratic checks and balances. Justice Minister Gabriel Aguilar has presented CACCO as part of a broader effort to reassert state control over the prison system, which he says has been infiltrated by organized crime. The first transfers to the prison will take place at the end of October. [USN:S0N3ST094 TEXT:"Fernandez recently told Reuters"] that greater US security presence would help Costa Rica confront drug trafficking and organized crime, although current coordination remains focused on patrols, investigations and extradition efforts.

item.title: Pope Leo back on his feet after shock cancer diagnosis
item.description: Pope Leo's recovery from surgery is progressing as expected and he has begun walking in his hospital room, the Vatican said.
item.dc:creator: CNA

Pope Leo back on his feet after shock cancer diagnosis

Pope Leo's recovery from surgery is progressing as expected and he has begun walking in his hospital room, the Vatican said.

Pope Leo arrives at Gemelli Hospital ahead of the pontiff's surgery to remove a lung nodule in Rome, Italy, on Oct 13, 2026. (Photo: Reuters/Guglielmo Mangiapane)

VATICAN CITY: Pope Leo 's recovery from surgery is progressing as expected and he has begun walking in his hospital room and eating normally, the Vatican said on Wednesday (Oct 14), after doctors announced the 71-year-old pontiff was being treated for lung cancer . World leaders, Catholics across the globe and senior cardinals at the Vatican have offered prayers for Pope Leo after he had part of his right lung removed in an operation on Tuesday. Blood tests and a chest X-ray carried out on Wednesday showed normal post-operative results, the Vatican said, adding that the pontiff had undergone respiratory physiotherapy. The cancer diagnosis for a pope known to be relatively young and energetic and who was elected only in May 2025 caused shock and raised questions about the future shape of his papacy as he deals with the illness.

Pope Leo normally follows a very busy schedule. He is due to make a tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru from Nov 6 to 17 and the Vatican press office said on Wednesday that "nothing has changed" regarding the planned trip. However, Peruvian President Keiko Fujimori said on Wednesday that the dates could change because of the amount of time his recovery would take. The pope is the ultimate earthly authority for the world 's 1.4 billion Catholics and does not have a deputy who steps in when he is sick. When a pope is incapacitated, the business of the Vatican's vast bureaucracy carries on as usual, holding off on any decisions that require papal approval.

PRAYERS FOR POPE LEO A prayer was recited for Pope Leo to have a good convalescence and complete healing during an open-air Mass in St Peter's Square on Wednesday following the surgery. The pope has been diagnosed with lung adenocarcinoma, the most common form of lung cancer , and doctors removed the lower lobe of his right lung during Tuesday's operation in an effort to eliminate all cancer ous tissue. Human lung s have five lobes - three in the right lung and two in the left. The operation lasted about 90 minutes and was completed without complications, the pope 's lead surgeon, Professor Stefano Margaritora, and his personal physician, Dr Luigi Carbone, said late on Tuesday. The Vatican has not disclosed the size of the tumour or whether the disease had spread to nearby lymph nodes, key factors in determining prognosis. Dr Serena Ricciardi, a lung cancer specialist at Rome's San Camillo Forlanini Hospital, said that if the cancer had not spread to Pope Leo 's lymph nodes, the surgery may have been sufficient for treatment. "If there are no further issues or lymph node involvement, we could consider the surgery curative," she told Reuters. "The disease has been completely removed." Pope Leo is relatively young for a Church leader. He enjoys sports, including tennis, and is not known to be a smoker or to have had recent health issues.

Related:

What we know about Pope Leo's lung cancer diagnosis

Pope Leo recovering after lung cancer operation

ENGAGEMENTS CANCELLED UNTIL NEXT WEEK The Vatican said this week that the pope was expected to remain in hospital for about a week and that all his public engagements had been cancelled until Oct 20. The Mass on Wednesday was the closing act of an assembly of bishops called by Pope Leo to discuss the Church's family life teachings, the largest gathering of Church leaders so far during this papacy. Filipino Cardinal Luis Tagle led the service in place of Pope Leo . The pope last week approved Tagle as the dean of the Church's College of Cardinals, in the first selection of an Asian cleric to the elite role. Political leaders offered messages of support. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said he and his wife Jeanette were praying for the pope , an American who was born in Chicago. "May the Lord give him strength and the Holy Spirit guide the medical professionals taking care of the Holy Father," he said on X. Rubio met Pope Leo at the Vatican in May. There was no immediate response on social media from US President Donald Trump, who has criticised the pope , or from Vice President JD Vance, who is a Catholic.

Source: Reuters/fs

item.title: US inflation heats up in September; Fed rate hike this month back on table
item.description: US inflation rose to 3.7 per cent in September, driven by higher gasoline prices, increasing pressure on households and complicating the Federal Reserve’s decision on interest rates.
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:
Advertisement

World

US inflation heats up in September; Fed rate hike this month back on table

US inflation rose to 3.7 per cent in September, driven by higher gasoline prices, increasing pressure on households and complicating the Federal Reserve’s decision on interest rates.

A motorist fills up his tank at a gas station amid a fuel shortage in Denpasar, Bali, Indonesia, Wednesday, Oct 14, 2026. (Photo: AP/Firdia Lisnawati)

WASHINGTON: US consumer prices accele rate d in September as the cost of gasoline surged, dealing another blow to US President Donald Trump and his Republican Party ahead of the Nov 3 midterm elections and putting an interest rate increase later this month back on the radar. The Consumer Price Index report from the Labour Department on Wednesday (Oct 14) showed a broadening of price pressures beyond energy, raising concerns among economists that underlying inflation could be getting sticky. Financial markets now see the Fed eral Reserve's interest rate decision this month as a closer call than before the data was released. The report added to surveys this month that showed a further deterioration in consumer sentiment and a plunge in Trump's approval rating, driven by angst over the rising cost of living. A Reuters/Ipsos poll showed about 78 per cent of Americans blamed Trump's policies, including tariffs on imports and the Middle East conflict, for rising prices, which are outpacing wages. "The inflation we're experiencing right now is largely the result of erratic policy from the executive branch," said Kyle Moore, chief economist at the Century Foundation, a progressive think tank.

"Worse still, the directionless war in Iran continues to disrupt global supply chains. This administration has also been wholly unwilling to moderate the pace of the AI and data-centre buildout." The CPI rose 0.6 per cent last month after climbing 0.4 per cent in Aug us t, the Labour Department's Bureau of Labour Statistics said. The increase in the CPI was in line with economists' expectations.  In the 12 month s through September , the CPI advanced 3.7 per cent after rising 3.4 per cent in Aug us t. A 9.1 per cent surge in gasoline prices accounted for more than half of the increase in the CPI over the month . The US-Israeli war with Iran is driving up energy prices. Other motor fuels, which include diesel, soared 11.9 per cent last month and were up 60.9 per cent on a year-over-year basis. Diesel prices at the pump are at record highs, and there are fears that those costs will soon feed through to higher prices at the supermarket. Food prices were unchanged after gaining 0.1 per cent in both July and Aug us t. Grocery store prices dipped 0.1 per cent over the month , but rose 1.8 per cent on a year-over-year basis. Beef prices dropped 1.0 per cent in September and the cost of dairy and related products eased 0.9 per cent. But prices for non-alcoholic beverages surged 0.9 per cent, while fruits and vege table s cost 0.5 per cent more.

CORE INFLATION ABOVE EXPECTATIONS Excluding the volatile food and energy components, the CPI gained 0.3 per cent in September , matching the gain in Aug us t. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast the so-called core CPI would rise 0.2 per cent. The core CPI was lifted by a 0.4 per cent increase in the cost of shelter, including hotel and motel rooms. Owners' equivalent rent rose 0.3 per cent. There were increases in the costs of recreation and education. Prices for us ed cars and trucks increased 0.7 per cent, while airline fares rose 1.2 per cent amid higher jet fuel prices. Apparel prices climbed 0.3 per cent. In the 12 month s through September , core CPI inflation increased 2.6 per cent after advancing 2.4 per cent in Aug us t. The US central bank tracks the Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index for its 2 per cent inflation target. The core CPI measure is lagging core PCE inflation , which increased 3.0 per cent in Aug us t, beca us e of the different weights assigned to the components in the baskets. Financial markets raised the chances of a rate hike at the Fed 's Oct 27 to 28 policy meeting to roughly 52 per cent from about 22 per cent prior to the CPI report, CME Gro up 's Fed Watch Tool showed. The odds of a rate increase this month had diminished following underwhelming payroll gains in September as well as cooler-than-expected PCE inflation readings for July and Aug us t.

Related:

New White House spokeswoman heavy on Trump praise, light on questions in debut

Dollar gains, Wall Street stocks fall after hot inflation data

US Treasury yields were mostly higher while the dollar advanced vers us a basket of currencies. US stocks opened lower. The Fed in September raised its overnight benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to the 3.75 per cent-4.00 per cent range, its first hike in three years, and flagged further increases in borrowing costs in the month s ahead. Economists had expected the Fed to raise rate s in December. The September CPI inflation report was keenly awaited by millions of retirees and other Social Security recipients trying to figure out how much their benefits will increase next year. The Social Security Administration announced a 3.6 per cent cost-of-living adj us tment for Social Security and S up plemental Security Income benefits for 2027. The programmes benefit older Americans who have retired as well as the disabled and certain widows, widowers and children.

Source: Reuters/fs

Ukrainian drones hit Russia's top data centre in attack on AI ambitions

The attack follows a series of Ukrainian strikes on Russian data centres.

MOSCOW: Ukrainian drones hit Russia's biggest data centre on Wednesday (Oct 14), part of a series of attack s appearing to target Moscow's ambitions to develop Russian artificial intelligence capabilities on a par with those from the US and China. The strike on the Balakovo data centre , owned by Sberbank, the country's largest bank and technology company, followed three attack s in the past week on data centre s owned by Russian technology group Yandex. "We confirm that the data processing centre was attack ed. At the same time, all of Sberbank's systems and services are operating normally and without disruption," Sberbank First Deputy CEO Alexander Vedyakhin told reporters. Russian President Vladimir Putin held a previously unannounced meeting on Wednesday with top officials on "information security", in which Sberbank CEO German Gref took part. The Kremlin s ai d that the meeting was not linked to the attack s on data centre s. Russia's state RIA Novosti news agency reported in 2024 that the Sberbank centre hit on Wednesday would host Russia's biggest supercomputer, which is scheduled to go into operation in 2027.

The Yandex data centre s, hit earlier, hosted all three of that company's operating supercomputers. Neither Yandex nor Sberbank has s ai d whether supercomputers, used to tr ai n the AI models, were damaged in the Ukrainian attack s. Along with Yandex, its m ai n domestic rival, Sberbank is Russia's leading developer of artificial intelligence. The domestic market is shared between Sberbank's GigaChat model and YandexGPT.

DIFFICULTIES PURCHASING CHIPS Both companies have invested heavily in the development of their models but lag global leaders in the United States and China by up to nine months, according to Sberbank's own estimates, partly due to Western sanctions which hinder Russia's access to the most advanced hardware. "It's clear what difficulties we face when purchasing modern graphics processing units. Both we and Yandex suffer from this," Gref s ai d on Sep 29, calling it the biggest reason why Russia lags behind the US and China in AI . Sberbank is in talks to buy chips from Chinese makers, but in an interview with Reuters on Jun 3, Vedyakhin s ai d that US chipmaker Nvidia's NVDA.O monopoly on its CUDA software platform, which has become an AI industry standard, is an even greater problem. Yandex s ai d previously that its supercomputers operated on Nvidia A100 chips, a model launched in 2020 and since then succeeded by more advanced H100 chips. Sberbank has two functioning supercomputers. The most advanced one, called Christofari Neo, ranked 167th in the Top 500 list of the world's most powerful supercomputers, is located in Moscow and is based on Nvidia A100 chips. Yandex's most advanced Chervonenkis supercomputer is ranked 101st in the same list. IT expert Mikh ai l Klimarev told Reuters it could take a long time to replace the chips due to Western sanctions, while damage to the supercomputers could set back the Russian AI industry, which already suffered from sanctions. "The equipment is being imported, but it's done at a high cost, through indirect routes. First, you need to negotiate so that someone is willing to sell it to you and is not afr ai d of sanctions," he s ai d.

Related:

Heavy Russian strikes on Ukraine kill 6, cut power in Kyiv

Russian strike on buses kills 30 in frontline Ukrainian city

NATO general sets out tough military response to any 'foolish' Russian attack

PROTECT ASSETS Some commentators compared the lack of reported disruption at state-controlled Sberbank with Yandex - whose taxi and food delivery units had reported disruptions - saying it showed that Sberbank's centre s are better protected. "This is a great example of what a business owner can do to protect their assets," wrote military blogger Alexander Kots. Under an August decree by Putin, the state can take over administration of poorly protected facilities. The Sberbank site is located close to the Balakovo nuclear power plant, which the data centre uses as an energy source, and the Saratov hydroelectric power plant. No damage was reported to either plant from the attack . Ukr ai ne says it is responding to Russian attack s on its own data sites. Both countries have attack ed each other's refineries, power stations, ports and e-commerce companies. Russia's digital development ministry s ai d this week it was in talks with the military on protecting the data centre s, while some lawmakers called for them to be moved underground where the hardware will be out of reach for drones . "We need a so-called Doomsday data vault," Valery Yermakov, deputy CEO of state-controlled Rostelecom, another major data centre operator, told a conference in Moscow.

Source: Reuters/fs

item.title: Banks, buildings burn as Albania's capital Tirana erupts into student violence
item.description: Tens of thousands of students stormed the streets of Tirana on Wednesday, setting alight a government building and two banks and hurling stones at police during a protest over rising education costs and corruption.
item.dc:creator: Fatos Bytyci
item.content:encoded: Tens of thousands of students stormed the streets of Tirana on Wednesday, setting alight a government building and two banks and hurling stones at police during a protest over rising education costs and corruption. Police responded with water cannons and tear gas to disperse protesters who started a fire at the ministry of education building, overturned garbage cans and smashed the fronts of local businesses, Reuters footage showed. A Raiffeisen Bank branch near the education ministry also caught fire, a Reuters witness said. The protests represent the most violent outburst against Prime Minister Edi Rama, who won a fourth term in office in elections in May last year but has since faced growing discontent at [USN:L6N3ZC0BA TEXT:"perceived graft"] surrounding top officials. Protesters also dismiss opposition figures as unpalatable alternatives. The unrest caps a summer of peaceful protests against Rama, triggered by the proposed development of a [USN:L6N4380FB TEXT:"luxury resort"] along Albania's pristine southern coast backed by US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner which has been [USN:L6N42J18T TEXT:"caught up in legal disputes"]. "This is a revolution. We are tired of peaceful protests. We will not stop until Rama resigns," said Lora, a student who declined to give her last name said as she threw rocks at the police. Others chanted "Resignation" and "Police of crime." WIDER PROTESTS Student organisers said the protest was over conditions at universities, higher education costs, a lack of financial support and employment prospects after graduation. The unrest is part of a broader wave of student activism sweeping Europe over education and living conditions. In France, high school students have staged [USN:L1N45U08J TEXT:"weeks of protests"] and school blockades demanding more teachers and better facilities, arguing that deteriorating school buildings and overcrowded classrooms are undermining education. Albanian media reported that Wednesday's protests spread to universities at Elbasan and Shkodra. The government condemned the violence. "Protesting is a legitimate right, but it cannot be used as an excuse for violence, city destruction or ugly fighting in the middle of the road," Deputy Prime Minister Albana Kociu said on Facebook. "I call on students and every honest citizen who believes in the right to protest: Distance yourself from violence and vandalism!" The police issued a statement calling for calm. "Any person who uses violence, burns or destroys property, or attacks Police officers, bears individual responsibility and will face the law, in accordance with the offences committed," it said.

GENEVA: Hospitals across Yemen are struggling to cope with a sharp rise in war casualties, while intensified fighting along multiple front lines has cut off aid to around 800,000 people, humanitarian agencies said on Wednesday (Oct 14).

Front-line hospitals in areas including Marib, Taiz and Yemen's Red Sea coast are seeing unprecedented numbers of weapon-wounded patients, with some facilities admitting more than 700 casualties in a single week, according to the Red Cross.

More than 200,000 people have been displaced from their homes since fighting in the country began in recent weeks, sparked by renewed fighting between the Iran-backed Houthi group and Saudi-backed government forces in Yemen, according to the United Nations' International Organization for Migration.

A displaced Yemeni child sits under a tree as families gather to receive aid at the Al-Fallahine displacement camp in Dar Saad district, Aden, Yemen on Oct 12, 2026. (Photo: AP/Abdulnasser Alseddik)

"Trauma care staff are under enormous pressure," ICRC health coordinator Feras Abusamra said in a statement. Only a small proportion of Yemen's functioning health facilities are capable of providing comprehensive trauma care, he said, while hospitals face large numbers of wounded people amid shortages of surgical supplies, anesthesia, oxygen and medicines.

Yemen's health services, battered by more than a decade of conflict, economic crisis, displacement and disease outbreaks, may have limited capacity to absorb a new surge in mass casualties if fighting intensifies further, the ICRC warned.

The fighting has also cut off life-saving humanitarian assistance for 800,000 people in Taiz - Yemen's third-largest city, which currently hosts the largest number of people fleeing the fighting - and other areas impacted by the conflict, the UN World Food Programme said on Wednesday.

Some districts are now inaccessible because of fighting and road closures, the WFP said, adding that wheat flour stocks are nearly exhausted and remaining food in local markets may last only a short time.

"This is the kind of situation that can rapidly spiral into a humanitarian catastrophe if assistance cannot move safely and reach those who need it most," said El-Khidir Daloum, WFP Representative and Country Director in Yemen, in a statement.

item.title: テンセントがオラクルからAI半導体10万個をリース、70億ドル規模－FT
item.description:
（ブルームバーグ）： 中国のテンセント・ホールディングス（騰訊）は、東南アジアでオラクルから先端のAI半導体を借り受けることで合意した。テンセントにとってAI半導体のリース契約としては過去最大規模となる。英紙フィナンシャル・タイムズ（FT）が事情に詳しい関係者の話として報じた。
報道によると、テンセントは、5年間の契約の一環として10万個の半導体を利用できるようになる。契約額は70億ドル（約1兆1000億円）に上るという。
中国のAI開発企業は米国の輸出規制を回避するため、米エヌビディア製など中国国内では入手できないAIアクセラレーターを海外で借りて利用している。中国のテクノロジー企業は、東南アジアのデータセンターの最大顧客層の一つとなっている。
テンセントとオラクルの担当者は、ブルームバーグ・ニュースのコメント要請に直ちに応じなかった。
原題：Tencent Leases AI Chips From Oracle
